docs.title: A canvas is a list of layers
docs.text:
A Canvas has a size and an ordered list of layers. Each layer method adds one layer and returns the canvas, so calls chain:

from quickthumb import Canvas

canvas = (
    Canvas(1280, 720)
    .background(color="#0F172A")
    .text(content="Hello", size=64, color="#FFFFFF", align="center")
    .outline(width=8, color="#22D3EE")
)
canvas.render("hello.png")

Layers are drawn in the order you add them. The first one is at the back and the last one is on top, so you describe an image the way you would paint it: background first, details last.

docs.title: Layer types
docs.text: Method Adds Reference .background() A full-canvas color, gradient, or image Background .text() Text, plain or as styled TextParts Text .image() A placed image, optionally cut out of its background Image .shape() A rectangle, ellipse, pill, triangle, star, or polygon Shape .svg() An SVG file such as an icon or logo (needs the svg extra) SVG .video() A video clip, for animated exports Video .chart(), .qr_code() A bar or line chart, or a QR code Data visualizations .counter() A number that counts from one value to another Canvas .group() A row or column that positions its children for you Group .outline() A border around the edge of the canvas Outline .custom(fn) Your own function that draws on the Pillow image Canvas

docs.title: Position and alignment
docs.text:
position is an (x, y) pair. Each value is pixels or a percentage of the canvas, and you can mix them:

canvas.shape(shape="rectangle", position=(64, 64), width=200, height=80, color="#CC0000")
canvas.text(content="Hello", size=72, color="#FFFFFF", position=("8%", 360))

align says which point of the layer sits at that position. By default it is the top-left corner. align=("center", "middle") puts the layer's center there instead, and align=("right", "bottom") with position=(1280, 720) pins a layer to the bottom-right corner of a 1280×720 canvas whatever its size.

align accepts several spellings of the same thing:

align=("center", "middle")      # (horizontal, vertical)
align="center"                  # same as ("center", "middle")
align="bottom-right"
align=Align.BOTTOM_RIGHT

Horizontal values are left, center, and right; vertical values are top, middle, and bottom. A text layer with align but no position is placed on the canvas by its alignment, so align="center" centers it.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Effects change how one layer is drawn. Pass them as a list:

from quickthumb import Shadow, Stroke

canvas.text(
    content="CLICK NOW",
    size=96,
    color="#FFFFFF",
    effects=[
        Stroke(width=4, color="#000000"),
        Shadow(offset_x=4, offset_y=4, color="#000000", blur_radius=8),
    ],
)

Not every effect makes sense on every layer:

Layer Effects Background Filter, Grain Text Stroke, Shadow, Glow, Background (a box behind the text) Shape Stroke, Shadow, Glow, InnerShadow, BackdropBlur Image, SVG, video Stroke, Shadow, Glow, Filter, Grain, Duotone, InnerShadow, BackdropBlur

Passing an effect a layer doesn't support raises ValidationError. The Effects reference lists every parameter.

docs.title: Rich text
docs.text:
A plain string is enough when all the text looks the same. To style parts of it differently, pass a list of TextParts:

from quickthumb import TextPart

canvas.text(
    content=[
        TextPart(text="5 ", color="#FBBF24"),
        TextPart(text="WAYS TO WIN", color="#FFFFFF"),
    ],
    size=80,
    weight=900,
    position=("8%", "55%"),
    align=("left", "middle"),
)

Settings on the layer (size, weight here) apply to every part unless the part sets its own. A part can override color, size, font, weight, bold, italic, letter_spacing, line_height, and effects.

docs.title: Gradients, blend modes, and fit
docs.text:
Backgrounds take a gradient as well as a color or an image:

from quickthumb import LinearGradient, RadialGradient

canvas.background(gradient=LinearGradient(angle=135, stops=[("#FF5733", 0.0), ("#3333FF", 1.0)]))
canvas.background(gradient=RadialGradient(center=(0.5, 0.5), stops=[("#FF5733", 0.0), ("#3333FF", 1.0)]))

Colors in stops can include alpha ("#00000080"), which is how you darken part of a photo behind text.

blend_mode on a background or image layer sets how it combines with what is underneath: normal, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, or lighten.

fit sets how an image fills its box: cover fills it and crops the excess (the default for backgrounds), contain fits the whole image inside, and fill stretches it.

docs.title: Auto layout
docs.text:
Text that is placed by hand breaks when the copy gets longer. A group measures its children and stacks them in a row or column; you place the group once and it places the children:

canvas.group(
    children=[
        {"type": "shape", "shape": "pill", "width": 120, "height": 36, "color": "#E94560"},
        {"type": "text", "content": "AUTO LAYOUT", "size": 96, "color": "#FFFFFF", "weight": 900},
        {"type": "text", "content": "Longer copy pushes the rest down", "size": 40, "color": "#A2A8D3"},
    ],
    direction="column",
    gap=24,
    position=("8%", "50%"),
    align=("left", "middle"),
)

Children don't set a position, and groups can contain groups. See Group.

docs.title: JSON specs
docs.text:
Everything above can be written as JSON instead of Python, and a canvas converts both ways:

spec = canvas.to_json()
same_canvas = Canvas.from_json(spec)

The only exception is .custom(fn), because a Python function can't be stored as JSON.

JSON specs can also define colors and sizes once in a theme block and refer to them as $theme.<path>:

{
  "kind": "canvas",
  "width": 1280,
  "height": 720,
  "theme": { "colors": { "primary": "#B8FF00" }, "sizes": { "title": 96 } },
  "layers": [
    { "type": "text", "content": "Hello", "size": "$theme.sizes.title", "color": "$theme.colors.primary" }
  ]
}

See JSON Schema & AI Workflow.

docs.title: Path motion
docs.text:
Canvas.path() supports SVG path data, fills (including gradients), and dashed strokes. A path's fixed width/height viewport clips its local drawing and defines its normalized anchor, including during rotation and scaling:

from quickthumb import AnimationSpec, Canvas, KeyframeSpec, ScaleTrack, TimingSpec

canvas = Canvas(320, 240).path(
    "M2 20C2 2 38 2 38 20C38 38 2 38 2 20Z", (100, 80), 40, 40,
    "#38B6A080", anchor=(0.5, 0.5),
    animation=AnimationSpec.timeline(
        ScaleTrack(keyframes=[KeyframeSpec(time=0, value=1), KeyframeSpec(time=1, value=4)]),
        timing=TimingSpec(duration=1), easing="linear",
    ),
)
frame = canvas.render_frame(0.75)

Use track timelines to animate a path. Support varies by output format; presets, stagger, Group children and transform parenting are not supported for paths. See the Path API for animation and export details.

docs.title: Errors and checks
docs.text:
Arguments are validated when you add a layer, before anything is drawn:

from quickthumb import ValidationError

try:
    canvas.text(content="Hello", size=64, color="#FFF")
except ValidationError as error:
    print(error)  # /color: invalid hex color: #FFF

Problems that only show up while drawing, such as a failed download, raise RenderingError, and a local file that doesn't exist raises MissingAssetError. Every error carries structured details; see Structured Errors.

A canvas can be valid and still look wrong. canvas.diagnose() looks for text that is too small or runs off the canvas, low contrast, layers hidden by other layers, and similar problems, without rendering a file. See Diagnostics & CLI.

docs.title: Diagnostics & CLI
docs.text:
quickthumb can check a design for common layout and legibility problems without rendering a file: from Python with canvas.diagnose(), or from the terminal with quickthumb lint.

To check a design in Python, start with the example below. For a JSON file, install the CLI and run quickthumb lint. Use quickthumb doctor to check export dependencies, or quickthumb render to write an output. The detailed finding rules and other CLI commands are below.

docs.title: canvas.diagnose()
docs.text:
Returns a DiagnosticReport whose findings list contains Diagnostic entries. An empty list means the checks found no issues; it does not guarantee visual quality or catch every problem. Review the rendered result as well.

from quickthumb import Canvas

with open("spec.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    canvas = Canvas.from_json(f.read())

for finding in canvas.diagnose().findings:
    print(finding.severity, finding.code, finding.message)

Each Diagnostic has stable human-readable fields and optional structured fields for automation:

Field Type Description code str One of "off-canvas", "tiny-text", "text-overflow", "text-clipped", "missing-glyph", "low-contrast", "layer-overlap", "layer-hidden", "edge-crowding", "near-alignment", "caption-safe-area", "caption-timing", "caption-overlap", "caption-reading-time", "clip-stretch", or "motion-path-unused-handle" severity str "warning" or "error" layer_index int Index of the offending layer in canvas.layers message str Human-readable explanation with the measured values layer_id str \| None Stable measured layer id, such as "layer:3" or "layer:3:0" for group children layer_name str \| None Layer name when the layer model exposes one bbox dict \| None Measured canvas-space bounding box with x, y, width, and height related_layers list[str] Layer ids involved in the finding measured dict Raw rule-specific values, such as contrast ratio, font size, or canvas dimensions suggestion str \| None Repair hint when the rule can provide one

docs.title: What gets checked
docs.text:
Code Trigger off-canvas A layer's bounding box falls partly or fully outside the canvas motion-path-unused-handle An incoming handle on the first position keyframe or outgoing handle on the last has no adjacent segment tiny-text Text smaller than 2.5% of the canvas height, likely unreadable at thumbnail size text-overflow A single word is wider than the layer's max_width and cannot be wrapped text-clipped Wrapped text extends past the canvas or its declared text box missing-glyph The selected font renders one or more characters as a missing-glyph placeholder low-contrast Text color has a contrast ratio under 2.0 against the composited layers below it layer-overlap Two visible layers overlap substantially enough to obscure one another layer-hidden A visible layer is fully covered by later opaque layers edge-crowding A visible layer is too close to a canvas safe margin or platform overlay near-alignment Related, unrotated layers have measured x/y starts within three pixels but are not exactly aligned caption-safe-area A video caption sits inside the canvas safe-area margin caption-timing A video caption ends after its clip does, so it is never seen caption-overlap Two video captions share both a moment and a rendered background caption-reading-time A cue is on screen under 0.8s, or runs past 20 display columns a second, leaving too little time to read it. Wide scripts such as Korean and Japanese count two columns per character while joiners and combining marks count none, and a cue that outlives its clip is measured over the part of it that is actually seen clip-stretch A clip plays slower than 0.5x or faster than 2x of its own rate. Usually it is being stretched to fit a scene, but a deliberate slow-motion or timelapse beat is reported the same way

With an LLM

Send the findings back to the model as specific edits to make, rather than asking for a new design. See AI Workflow.

Near-alignment checks compare rendered layer positions to spot unintended 1–3 pixel misalignments.

Contrast and Alignment Checks

  • Contrast checks sample text against the composited background beneath it, including any Background pill effects attached to the text layer.
  • Near-alignment flags layers that are almost aligned (within 3px) so you can snap them cleanly without guessing coordinates.

docs.title: The quickthumb CLI
docs.text:
The CLI requires the cli extra:

pip install "quickthumb[cli]"

docs.title: quickthumb inspect
docs.text:
Inspect a Canvas or Deck JSON spec without writing an export:

quickthumb inspect spec.json
quickthumb inspect deck.json --format json
quickthumb inspect deck.json --target video --fps 24 --max-samples 100
quickthumb inspect spec.json --reduced-motion --var title="Hello"

Text output includes ordered page/layer bounds, per-layer motion durations and event counts, capability/fallback rows, observed assets, and layout diagnostics. --format json emits exactly the Python inspect_document() result envelope, including version and document kind. It has the same page ordering and common fields for both document kinds, so scripts can consume it without guessing the input type.

--target selects a capability family (raster, html, pptx, or video); omitting it reports all four. --fps and --max-samples control bounded motion property observations, not image-frame generation. --reduced-motion inspects the accessible static policy. --var KEY=VALUE follows the other spec commands.

Inspection can resolve fonts/assets or decode media for measurement. It reports observed asset states and does not perform a separate prefetch or readiness check. Motion-inspection duration is not an encoded-video duration; use the Python sample() timeline for canonical frame and playback timing.

Findings are informational: successful inspection exits 0 even with warnings. Input, validation, and missing-asset errors exit 1; rendering/export-category errors (including an empty Deck's motion inspection) exit 2. With JSON output, these errors use the existing {"errors": [...]} structured envelope. Use lint --fail-on to gate on diagnostics and doctor to check environment readiness. Argument-parsing errors, such as --fps abc, still use Typer's standard text on stderr and exit 2; the JSON error envelope applies after argument parsing.

docs.title: quickthumb lint
docs.text:
Checks a JSON spec for the same findings as diagnose():

quickthumb lint spec.json
quickthumb lint spec.json --format json
quickthumb diagnose spec.json --format json

[warning] layer 3: tiny-text: text size 14px is below 18px (2.5% of canvas height) ...
[warning] layer 4: low-contrast: text contrast ratio 1.47 against the layers below it ...

With --format json, lint prints a machine-readable payload:

{
  "summary": {
    "diagnostic_count": 1,
    "error_count": 0,
    "warning_count": 1
  },
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "code": "tiny-text",
      "severity": "warning",
      "layer_index": 3,
      "message": "text size 14px is below 18px ...",
      "layer_id": "layer:3",
      "bbox": {"x": 80, "y": 64, "width": 120, "height": 17},
      "related_layers": ["layer:3"],
      "measured": {"font_size": 14, "threshold": 18.0},
      "suggestion": "increase text size to at least 18px"
    }
  ]
}

lint exits with a status that CI can act on:

Exit code Meaning 0 No issues found 1 Invalid spec (bad JSON, validation error, missing asset, invalid option) 2 Rendering failure 3 Findings reported

diagnose is an alias for lint. Both commands accept the same automation options:

quickthumb lint spec.json --fail-on error
quickthumb lint spec.json --ignore edge-crowding --ignore missing-glyph

--fail-on warning (the default) exits 3 for any remaining finding. --fail-on error allows warnings while still failing on errors, and --fail-on never always exits 0 after printing the findings. --ignore removes matching diagnostic codes from both the output and the exit-status calculation. Invalid specs with --format json emit an errors list of structured error details rather than a traceback.

JSON inputs must declare a top-level kind discriminator (canvas or deck). Deck findings include slide_index and retain the originating layer id, bounding box, measurements, related layers, and suggestion.

docs.title: quickthumb diff
docs.text:
Compare a rendered image with a golden image before accepting a visual change:

quickthumb diff golden.png output.png
quickthumb diff golden.png output.png --format json --output diff.png

The comparison combines an average perceptual hash with pixel-level metrics. By default, per-channel differences of up to 2 are ignored, but any pixel that exceeds that tolerance fails the comparison. The default perceptual-hash similarity threshold is 0.95. Tighten or relax those values for a particular renderer:

quickthumb diff golden.png output.png \
  --threshold 0.98 \
  --pixel-tolerance 1 \
  --max-diff-ratio 0.005

Use --format json for CI or agent pipelines. --max-diff-ratio can allow a small fraction of pixels to differ, and --output writes a pixel-difference image for visual inspection. Exit codes are:

Exit code Meaning 0 Images match within the configured tolerances 1 Images differ, inputs are invalid, or output cannot be written

The same comparison is available as a Python assertion:

from quickthumb import assert_image_similar

assert_image_similar(
    "golden.png",
    "output.png",
    threshold=0.95,
)

The assertion returns an ImageDiff with image sizes, changed-pixel counts, normalized mean error, perceptual hashes, and similarity metrics when callers need to report more detail.

docs.title: quickthumb render
docs.text:
Renders a JSON spec to an image file:

quickthumb render spec.json -o thumbnail.png
quickthumb render spec.json -o thumbnail.webp --format WEBP --quality 90
quickthumb render spec.json -o debug.png --debug
Option Description -o, --output Output file path (default output.png) --format PNG, JPEG, or WEBP --quality Compression quality: JPEG 1–95, WebP 1–100; not a rendering-quality control --debug Overlay public layer-id bounding boxes on raster output --var KEY=VALUE Substitute $KEY placeholders in the spec (repeatable) --error-format text (default) or json; see Structured Errors

render exits 1 for invalid specs, missing assets, and invalid options, and 2 for export failures such as an unsupported output format.

docs.title: quickthumb watch
docs.text:
Re-renders the spec every time the file changes, which is handy while adjusting a layout by hand:

quickthumb watch spec.json -o preview.png

watch takes the same options as render except --error-format; failures are printed as text and watching continues.

docs.title: quickthumb doctor
docs.text:
Discovers packages, tools, source requirements and output permissions before an export:

quickthumb doctor pdf -o out/thumbnail.pdf
quickthumb doctor mp4 --spec spec.json --format json

The workflow is one of png, jpeg, webp, gif, svg, html, pdf, pptx, mp4, webm, or mov. With --spec, the spec's plugin renderers, fonts, SVG/video layers, background removal, and remote assets add their own requirements. -o checks that the output location is writable (nothing is created).

Each finding is ok, warning (an optional limitation, such as a missing font or an unusable asset cache), or error (a required failure, such as a missing quickthumb[pdf] extra, ffmpeg, an unregistered plugin, or an unwritable output). Every warning and error includes a fix/remedy. Plugins are checked against the registry of the CLI process, which only has plugins registered at import time, so a spec that uses code-registered plugins will report them as unregistered. Exit code is 0 when no required check failed and 1 otherwise.

A successful report is not an export or fidelity certificate. Package discovery does not prove that native Cairo can load, and finding FFmpeg does not prove that its build has the encoder your output needs. doctor does not render or compare output. Run the intended export and inspect its receipt and file; use an explicit fidelity policy or quickthumb diff when visual comparison matters.

docs.title: quickthumb serve
docs.text:
Runs a local HTML slideshow server with live reload. With no source argument it looks for slides.py, slides.json, slides.html, or slides.htm in that order:

quickthumb serve
quickthumb serve examples/investor_deck.py
quickthumb serve deck.json --port 4040 --no-open

A Python source should define one module-level Deck or Canvas as deck, slides, or canvas. A JSON source must declare kind: "canvas" or kind: "deck"; Canvas documents contain layers, while Deck documents contain a top-level slides list. Use --host and --port to change the listening address, --no-open to suppress the initial browser window, and repeat --var KEY=VALUE for JSON template substitutions.

The audience view is /. Presenter mode is selected by the ?presenter query:

http://localhost:3030/?presenter

Presenter mode uses the same light theme as the preview: current slide and notes on the left, next slide and pause/resume/reset timer on the right, and simple navigation below. Slide previews retain their original proportions. Its navigation and per-slide animation progress are broadcast to audience tabs opened from the same server and restored on reload. Audience-only navigation remains local. Add notes in Python with .slide(canvas, notes="...") or as a notes string on a JSON slide.

docs.title: Timeline scrubber
docs.text:
Open the raster timeline while authoring Python or JSON documents:

quickthumb serve examples/timeline_preview.py --timeline
quickthumb serve deck.json --timeline --no-open

The timeline is also available at http://localhost:3030/timeline alongside an ordinary serve session. The default remains the HTML presentation, including slide navigation, click-triggered animations and synchronized presenter controls. Presentation and Inspect motion share the same slide selection and thumbnail navigation. Presentation keeps the slide central at its original aspect ratio; Inspect motion opens a frame-scrubbing panel below it. Presenter opens the synchronized speaker view, while Present opens the HTML slide fullscreen. Motion notes explain when HTML output is static or approximated. These controls are local authoring tools and are not added to exported HTML. Standalone HTML has no source document to sample; use its Python or JSON source for the timeline instead.

Inspection shows export-renderer frames without playback, audio or editing. Its seek position is independent of presenter/audience synchronization.

  • Drag the time slider, enter seconds, or click a slide/transition/motion boundary
  • Proxy limits the output's longest edge to 640 pixels (1080×1920 becomes 360×640), preparing reusable layer imagery and compositing ordinary motion on reduced surfaces. Later mixed-size slides fit that same output rectangle
  • Full shows native first-slide dimensions, using the same standard-quality canonical timeline sampler as Canvas.sample(time=...) / Deck.sample(time=...)
  • Source saves reload the timeline, preserving the selected resolution and time in the URL fragment and clamping the time if the new timeline is shorter
  • Only one browser frame request runs at a time; rapid seeks replace pending work with the latest choice. The displayed-frame label continues to identify the old frame until the requested frame is ready. Broken edits show an error and recover after the next save

The timeline scrubber renders instantaneous frame previews matching your export timing:

  • Proxy mode: Renders downscaled frames (up to 640px) for smooth, rapid seeking.
  • Full mode: Renders full-resolution frames matching standard export quality.
  • Note that audio playback is disabled during timeline scrubbing.

Local Security

quickthumb serve runs local Python and JSON files on your machine. Keep the default loopback address (127.0.0.1) when previewing untrusted content.

docs.title: Variable substitution
docs.text:
The JSON-based commands accept --var to fill $KEY (or ${KEY}) placeholders before parsing:

quickthumb render template.json -o ep42.png \
  --var TITLE="EPISODE 42" \
  --var ACCENT="#B8FF00"

Unresolved placeholders cause exit code 1. $theme.* references are not variables; they are resolved by the theme block inside the spec itself.

docs.title: Structured Errors
docs.text: Every quickthumb failure (an invalid field, a missing asset, an export a target cannot perform, or a bad command-line option) carries the same machine-readable detail. Agents can locate the offending input and choose a remedy without parsing prose; people still get a clear one-line message.

docs.title: Error detail fields
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning code string Stable identifier for the kind of failure (see codes) category string validation, asset, export, or input message string Human-readable description of the failure path string or null RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the input document, when the failure has a document location layer_id string or null Id of the innermost layer containing path, when one is known suggestion string or null Concrete remedy, when one is known

path is relative to the document being parsed or validated. For Canvas.from_json, Deck.from_json, validate(), and the CLI that is the document root, so Deck failures start with /slides/<index>. For a model built directly in Python, such as TextLayer(...), it is relative to that model.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
All quickthumb exceptions derive from QuickthumbError and expose the same details:

from quickthumb import Canvas, QuickthumbError

try:
    Canvas.from_json(spec).render("out.png")
except QuickthumbError as error:
    for detail in error.details:
        print(detail.code, detail.path, detail.layer_id, detail.suggestion)
    print(error)  # "/layers/1/max_width (layer 'title'): max_width must be positive"
Exception Category Raised for ValidationError validation Invalid JSON, unknown or missing fields, invalid values MissingAssetError asset A local image, SVG, video, text-fill, or audio file does not exist; also a FileNotFoundError RenderingError export Unsupported output formats, capabilities a target cannot export, renderer failures InputError input Invalid command-line options or unreadable spec files

Canvas.validate() and Deck.validate() return the same ErrorDetail records in ValidationReport.errors, so a pre-flight check and a failed render describe a problem identically.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
quickthumb render accepts --error-format json; quickthumb lint and quickthumb diagnose use their --format json option. Failures are written to stdout as one envelope with every detail field present:

quickthumb render spec.json -o out.png --error-format json

{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "asset_missing",
      "category": "asset",
      "message": "Asset not found: 'hero.png'",
      "path": "/slides/1/layers/0/path",
      "layer_id": "hero",
      "suggestion": "check the path relative to the working directory or use an http(s) URL"
    }
  ]
}

Text mode prints one line per detail to stderr, leading with the code:

error[asset_missing] /slides/1/layers/0/path (layer 'hero'): Asset not found: 'hero.png'. Suggestion: check the path relative to the working directory or use an http(s) URL.

Exit codes follow the category: export failures exit 2; validation, asset, and input failures exit 1.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
Code Category Meaning invalid_json validation The document is not valid JSON invalid_document validation The document is structurally unusable (for example, a Deck with no slides) invalid_field validation A field value has the wrong type or is out of range missing_field validation A required field is absent unknown_field validation A field is not part of the schema unknown_plugin validation A plugin layer names a renderer that is not registered asset_missing asset A referenced local file does not exist unsupported_format export The output extension is not an export format unsupported_capability export The target can't do what the document asks: a plugin layer is rendered (quickthumb can validate plugin layers but not draw them yet), or the export policy forbids a fallback the target needs (for example, ExportPolicy(unsupported_motion="error")) missing_dependency export An external tool such as FFmpeg is unavailable export_failed export Any other export or rendering failure, including an output path that cannot be written invalid_option input A command-line option value is invalid input_unreadable input The spec file cannot be read unresolved_variable input A $KEY placeholder has no matching --var

Codes are stable. Messages may be reworded, so automation should branch on code and path rather than on message.

docs.title: Which Python versions are supported?
docs.text: Python 3.11 or later. The package is classified for 3.11 and 3.12, and CI runs on 3.11. This includes background removal (the rembg extra).

docs.title: The quickthumb command isn't found
docs.text: The command line tool is an optional extra: pip install "quickthumb[cli]". Installation lists every extra.

docs.title: Why does my SVG layer raise RenderingError?
docs.text: Drawing SVG files needs the svg extra: pip install "quickthumb[svg]". Exporting a canvas to SVG doesn't.

docs.title: What happens if I render a canvas with no layers?
docs.text: You get a fully transparent image of the canvas size. It isn't an error.

docs.title: Why does a group child raise "group children must not set position"?
docs.text:
A group positions its children itself. Remove position from the child and place the group instead:

canvas.group(
    children=[{"type": "text", "content": "TITLE", "size": 96, "color": "#FFFFFF"}],
    position=("8%", "50%"),
    align=("left", "middle"),
)

A child's align is ignored too. Use the group's item_align to line children up across the group.

docs.title: How do I check a design for problems before rendering?
docs.text: Call canvas.diagnose(), or run quickthumb lint spec.json on a JSON spec. It reports text that is too small or off the canvas, low contrast, hidden layers, and more. See Diagnostics & CLI.

docs.title: My text runs off the canvas
docs.text:
Set max_width so it wraps:

canvas.text(content="A longer title that needs two lines", size=72, color="#FFFFFF", max_width="60%")

Add auto_scale=True (with max_width, max_height, or both) to shrink the text until it fits instead.

docs.title: I set bold=True and weight=900 and got an error
docs.text: They set the same thing, so use one. weight is more precise: TextPart(text="STRONG", weight=900).

docs.title: How do I use a Google Font?
docs.text:
Name it and set font_source="google". It is downloaded once and cached, and weight picks the matching file:

canvas.text(content="Hello", font="Inter", font_source="google", weight=800, size=72, color="#FFFFFF")

You can also pass the URL of a font file, or point QUICKTHUMB_FONT_DIR at a folder of fonts. See Webfonts & Background Removal.

docs.title: Can I use images from a URL?
docs.text: Yes. background(image=...) and image(path=...) accept http(s) URLs. They are downloaded and cached while rendering. To control the cache, see Remote assets and caching.

docs.title: How do I remove the background behind a person?
docs.text:
Set remove_background=True on the image layer. It needs the rembg extra:

canvas.image(path="portrait.jpg", position=("75%", "55%"), width=420, height=520, remove_background=True)

docs.title: What's the difference between cover, contain, and fill?
docs.text: cover fills the box and crops what doesn't fit. contain fits the whole image inside the box and leaves empty space. fill stretches the image to the box, ignoring its proportions.

docs.title: Which formats can I export?
docs.text:
The format comes from the file extension you pass to render():

Kind Formats Needs Images PNG, JPEG, WebP Vector and documents SVG, PDF, PPTX pdf / pptx extras for PDF and PPTX Web HTML Animation GIF, MP4, WebM ffmpeg for MP4 and WebM

See Choose an output format for a first export and the export reference for what each format keeps and loses.

docs.title: Can I set quality for a PNG?
docs.text: No. quality only applies to JPEG and WebP; passing it for PNG raises RenderingError.

docs.title: How do I get the image without writing a file?
docs.text:
png_base64 = canvas.to_base64(format="PNG")
jpeg_data_url = canvas.to_data_url(format="JPEG", quality=90)

docs.title: Can I pass a dict to Canvas.from_json()?
docs.text: No, it takes a JSON string. Convert first with json.dumps(data).

docs.title: Why does to_json() raise ValidationError?
docs.text: The canvas has a .custom(fn) layer. A Python function can't be written to JSON, so remove that layer first.

docs.title: My theme block disappeared after to_json()
docs.text: Theme tokens are replaced with their values when the spec is loaded, so to_json() writes the values and no theme block. Keep your original spec file if you want to keep editing the tokens.

docs.title: What do the different errors mean?
docs.text:
• ValidationError: an argument or spec field is invalid. Raised as soon as you add the layer or load the spec.
  • RenderingError: something failed while drawing, such as a download.
  • MissingAssetError: a local file the spec refers to doesn't exist.

Every error has details with a stable code, the JSON Pointer of the field, and the layer id. See Structured Errors.

docs.title: Render your first cards
docs.text: Build one episode-card layout and render it with three sets of content. Then change a title to make your own version.

docs.title: 1. Install quickthumb
docs.text:
You need Python 3.11 or later. In your Python environment:

python -m pip install quickthumb

If you need an environment first, follow Installation, then return here. The example uses only the base package and its built-in font: no font downloads, photos, or optional renderers are needed after installation.

docs.title: 2. Save and run the layout
docs.text:
Save this as episode_cards.py in your working directory, outside any quickthumb checkout:

from quickthumb import Canvas, Stroke

INK = "#111111"
WHITE = "#FFFFFF"


def episode_card(episode, title, accent):
    return (
        Canvas(1280, 720)
        .background(color=INK)
        .shape("rectangle", position=(0, 0), width=1280, height=360, color=accent)
        # The numeral stands on the band and crops at the top edge.
        .text(
            str(episode),
            size=540,
            color=INK,
            # A stroke in the text color thickens the regular-weight built-in font.
            effects=[Stroke(width=8, color=INK)],
            position=(1240, 360),
            align=("right", "bottom"),
            letter_spacing=-10,
        )
        .text(
            "THE BUILDER'S\nNOTEBOOK",
            size=26,
            color=INK,
            effects=[Stroke(width=1, color=INK)],
            position=(48, 44),
            letter_spacing=1,
        )
        .text(
            "EPISODE",
            size=26,
            color=INK,
            effects=[Stroke(width=1, color=INK)],
            position=(48, 330),
            align=("left", "bottom"),
            letter_spacing=1,
        )
        .text(
            title,
            size=136,
            color=WHITE,
            effects=[Stroke(width=2, color=WHITE)],
            position=(48, 688),
            align=("left", "bottom"),
            max_width=1184,
            max_height=290,
            auto_scale=True,
            balance_lines=True,
            line_height=1.04,
        )
    )


episodes = [
    (12, "Ship your first release", "#FF4B1F"),
    (13, "Make room for better work", "#FFD400"),
    (14, "Build less. Finish more.", "#4D8DFF"),
]

for episode, title, accent in episodes:
    episode_card(episode, title, accent).render(f"episode-{episode}.png")

Run it from that directory:

python episode_cards.py

Open episode-12.png, episode-13.png, and episode-14.png in the same directory. Each is a 1280 × 720 image. The script writes to those filenames each time it runs, replacing any existing files with those names.

docs.title: 3. Make the next card
docs.text:
Add another row to episodes, keeping the function unchanged:

(15, "Your next big idea", "#FF4B1F"),

Run the script again and open episode-15.png. You have reused the same layout with a new episode number, title, and color.

The title wraps within max_width. auto_scale=True lets it shrink to fit the specified width and height. Check your longest real titles before using the layout for a batch.

docs.title: Adapt the design
docs.text:
Inside episode_card(), change the colors, the numeral or title size, or the positions once to update every card. Layers are drawn in the order you add them. For your own typeface, add a local font path to each .text() call, such as font="/path/to/your-font.ttf", and remove the Stroke effects if the font is already heavy enough.

When expanding the layout, use canvas.diagnose() to check for common problems such as off-canvas layers and low contrast. This layout reports one off-canvas finding because the numeral is cropped on purpose. See Diagnostics for checks and their limits; a clean report does not establish that a design looks good.

  • JSON & AI Workflow: load and validate layouts as JSON.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: quickthumb needs Python 3.11 or later.

docs.title: Isolated environment
docs.text:
Install quickthumb 0.8.0 in a virtual environment outside any quickthumb checkout:

mkdir -p quickthumb-first-export
cd quickthumb-first-export
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install "quickthumb==0.8.0"

On Windows, activate with .venv\Scripts\activate instead. The shell commands above use Bash/Zsh. Installing dependencies needs the package index or a populated local cache. Running outside the checkout ensures Python imports the installed wheel rather than the source directory.

docs.title: Existing uv project
docs.text:
uv add "quickthumb[cli]>=0.8.0"

The base package is enough for PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, SVG output, and HTML. Try rendering your first episode cards before adding optional renderers. The example needs no font or image downloads after installation.

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Some features need extra packages. Install them by name, for example pip install "quickthumb[svg,pdf]".

Extra Use it for svg Drawing SVG files as layers. Exporting to SVG does not need this extra. pdf PDF export and optional PDF fidelity checks. pptx PowerPoint export. lottie Supported text outlines in Canvas Lottie exports; shape-only Lottie does not need it. rembg Removing image backgrounds. The first use downloads a model of about 170 MB. cli The quickthumb command, including render, lint, watch, and doctor.

MP4, WebM, and MOV export also need ffmpeg, which is a system program rather than a Python package:

brew install ffmpeg      # macOS
sudo apt install ffmpeg  # Debian / Ubuntu

MOV requires an FFmpeg build with the prores_ks encoder.

SVG layers also need the native Cairo library; the Python extra does not install system libraries. See CairoSVG installation for platform requirements.

docs.title: Check your environment
docs.text:
quickthumb doctor (from the cli extra) discovers requirements for an export:

quickthumb doctor            # PNG, the default
quickthumb doctor mp4        # discover ffmpeg/ffprobe
quickthumb doctor pdf --spec card.json -o out/card.pdf

It exits with status 1 if a required check fails, so it also works as a CI step. It does not render a test file or certify native libraries, codec support, or visual fidelity. Run the intended export as well. See Diagnostics & CLI for details.

docs.title: Development checkout
docs.text: To try unreleased changes, run uv build in the repository, then install the resulting wheel into the isolated environment using its absolute path, for example python -m pip install "/path/to/dist/quickthumb-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl[cli]". This installs the checkout's code rather than downloading the published release. See the 0.8.0 migration notes when upgrading from 0.7.0.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
All optional.

Variable What it does QUICKTHUMB_FONT_DIR Folder of font files to search when font is a family name QUICKTHUMB_DEFAULT_FONT Font to use when a text layer has no font QUICKTHUMB_FONT_CACHE_DIR Where downloaded fonts are cached (default: the system temp folder) QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_CACHE_DIR Where downloaded images are cached (default: the system temp folder) QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_MAX_AGE Seconds before a cached download is refreshed. Unset means never. QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_OFFLINE Set to 1 to never download; only cached files are used QUICKTHUMB_FFMPEG, QUICKTHUMB_FFPROBE Paths to ffmpeg and ffprobe if they aren't on PATH

Remote assets and caching explains the cache in more detail.

docs.title: JSON Schema & AI Workflow
docs.text:
Any quickthumb canvas can be written as JSON. A JSON spec can be generated by an LLM or a template, stored in a database, sent through an API, or kept in version control next to your content.

To generate, validate, and render a first spec, follow the AI workflow. Use this page to look up layer fields, effects, or the published schema. The quickthumb command requires pip install "quickthumb[cli]"; Python schema helpers work without the CLI extra.

docs.title: Round-trip serialization
docs.text:
Canonical JSON stores the authored document, separately from an export receipt:

from pathlib import Path

from quickthumb import Canvas

# Python → JSON
canvas = Canvas(320, 180).background(color="#102030")
json_str = canvas.to_json()
Path("scene.json").write_text(json_str, encoding="utf-8")

# JSON → Python
restored = Canvas.from_json(Path("scene.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
assert restored.to_json() == json_str
restored.export("from-json.png")

Note

Canvas.from_json() expects a JSON string. If you have a Python dict, call json.dumps(data) first. Canvases with .custom(fn) layers can't be serialized, because a Python function can't be stored as JSON.

Canonical serialization is deterministic for the same resolved document. It does not package fonts, images, media or cached downloads: retain referenced files and make their paths available when rendering elsewhere. Plugin JSON retains declared parameters and asset references, not Python callbacks; supply the matching explicit registry when loading it. Identical scene JSON does not guarantee identical pixels across fonts, renderer versions or platforms.

docs.title: JSON structure
docs.text:
A Canvas JSON document has four required top-level fields, plus an optional theme block:

{
  "kind": "canvas",
  "width": 1280,
  "height": 720,
  "theme": { ... },
  "layers": [ ... ]
}

The top-level "kind" discriminator is required (by Canvas.from_json(), Deck.from_json(), and the CLI) and must be "canvas" or "deck". Canvas documents carry layers; Deck documents carry slides and may also define a shared default size, theme, and transitions. Every layer object requires its own "type" discriminator field. Layers render in array order: the first item is at the back. Layer identity, placement, alignment and motion use the same shared vocabulary in Python, a Canvas JSON root and every Deck slide. A Deck does not introduce a different layer schema.

docs.title: Published schema
docs.text:
Emit the current JSON Schema from the same Pydantic models used by Canvas.from_json():

quickthumb schema > quickthumb.schema.json
quickthumb schema --output quickthumb.schema.json
quickthumb schema --document --output quickthumb.document-schema.json

The same schemas are available from Python as canvas_json_schema() and document_json_schema(), and hosted with these docs:

  • https://quickthumb.solaqua.dev/schema.json (Canvas)
  • https://quickthumb.solaqua.dev/document-schema.json (Canvas or Deck)

To get completion and validation while editing specs in VS Code, map your spec files to the hosted schema in .vscode/settings.json:

{
  "json.schemas": [
    {
      "fileMatch": ["*.thumb.json"],
      "url": "https://quickthumb.solaqua.dev/schema.json"
    }
  ]
}

Use a file mapping like this rather than a "$schema" key inside the spec: Canvas.from_json() rejects unknown top-level fields, including $schema.

The hosted files are regenerated on every docs deploy, which follows the main branch. Run quickthumb schema to get the schema for the version you have installed.

Schema scope

quickthumb schema describes concrete Canvas specs for external tooling and constrained generation. Use quickthumb schema --document for the combined Canvas/Deck discriminator schema. Canvas.from_json() remains the source of truth for what quickthumb can load.

The CLI, serve, Canvas.from_json(), and Deck.from_json() all require the matching top-level kind discriminator. Newly serialized documents include the discriminator at every document boundary, including Deck slides.

Deck slides may omit width and height when the Deck supplies default dimensions; the document schema accepts that form and canonical JSON emits the inherited dimensions on each slide. Transition objects use the same discriminated, strict contract as Deck.from_json().

Authoring conveniences such as $theme.* are resolved by quickthumb before model validation, so generic JSON Schema validators may reject unresolved authoring specs that quickthumb itself can load.

The command writes deterministic JSON only, so it can be checked into a repo, piped into an editor, or passed directly to a constrained-generation API. The Canvas schema includes the current canvas fields, built-in layer discriminators, effects, animations, supported platform presets, and the optional top-level theme block. The --document schema adds the Deck root and maps both document kinds through kind.

docs.title: Plugin layers
docs.text:
Plugin registrations are kept in one explicit PluginRegistry. A registration describes a layer type and its parameters. A separate trusted synchronous raster callback renders plugin layers as canonical RGBA pixels. Callbacks are application code, never serialized or imported from JSON.

from quickthumb import Canvas, PluginRegistry, canvas_json_schema

registry = PluginRegistry()
registry.register(
    "brand_badge",
    "1.0",
    params_schema={
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["label"],
        "properties": {"label": {"type": "string"}},
        "additionalProperties": False,
    },
)

canvas = Canvas.from_json(text, registry=registry)
schema = canvas_json_schema(registry=registry)

A plugin layer requires type: "plugin", renderer, version, object-valued params, and positive integer width/height. position accepts the normal pixel/percentage coordinates; align and opacity affect its local box. Standard clip and mask boundaries apply after rendering. A Group controls child placement and can animate the whole group, including static plugin pixels. The same explicit registry must be supplied to document parsers and Schema helpers.

from PIL import Image

def badge(params, context):
    with Image.new("RGBA", context.size, params["color"]) as image:
        return image.tobytes()

registry.register("badge", "1", raster=badge)
canvas = Canvas(320, 180, registry=registry).plugin(
    "badge", version="1", params={"color": "#42CEB7"},
    position=(20, 30), width=120, height=40,
)
canvas.export("badge.png")

The raster callback receives a params dict and context.size, returning raw RGBA8 bytes (width * height * 4). Declare external assets via assets={"texture": "assets/texture.png"} on the layer and access them with context.read_asset("texture").

docs.title: Optional native SVG
docs.text:
For vector outputs, register an optional svg= callback returning an SVG string:

def badge_svg(params, context):
    width, height = context.size
    return (
        f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}">'
        f'<rect width="{width}" height="{height}" fill="{params["color"]}"/></svg>'
    )

registry.register("badge", "1", raster=badge, svg=badge_svg)

In formats that don't support native SVG plugins, the layer automatically falls back to rendering via its raster callback.

docs.title: Plugin params Schema v1
docs.text:
params_schema accepts the documented quickthumb plugin-params v1 subset. It supports the JSON types object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, and null; required, properties, additionalProperties, items; const, enum, oneOf, anyOf; string patterns and size limits; and numeric minimum/maximum limits. Unsupported keywords such as $ref, allOf, and not are rejected during registration so the published Schema and runtime validation stay in agreement.

The process-global plugin_registry remains available for applications that want a shared default. For tests, services, and libraries, prefer an explicit PluginRegistry so registrations stay isolated and reproducible.

For constrained generation, prefer concrete resolved values in typed fields:

Use quickthumb.schema.json as the JSON response schema.
Generate one valid quickthumb canvas spec for a 1280x720 YouTube thumbnail.
Return only the JSON object.
Use concrete hex colors and numeric sizes in layer fields.
Use only these layer type discriminators: background, text, image, shape, svg, group, outline.

docs.title: Theme tokens
docs.text:
Define brand tokens once in a top-level theme block and reference them anywhere in the spec with $theme.path:

{
  "kind": "canvas",
  "width": 1280,
  "height": 720,
  "theme": {
    "colors": { "primary": "#B8FF00", "ink": "#111111" },
    "sizes": { "title": 96 }
  },
  "layers": [
    { "type": "background", "color": "$theme.colors.ink" },
    { "type": "text", "content": "Hello", "size": "$theme.sizes.title", "color": "$theme.colors.primary" }
  ]
}

Rules:

  • The theme block can nest groups arbitrarily; reference paths with dots: $theme.colors.primary.
  • A whole-string reference keeps its native JSON type: "size": "$theme.sizes.title" resolves to the number 96, and tokens can hold lists too.
  • Scalar tokens (strings, numbers) can also be embedded inside longer strings.
  • Theme values may reference other theme tokens (aliases). Circular references raise ValidationError.
  • Referencing an undefined token raises ValidationError.
  • Tokens are resolved at parse time: to_json() emits resolved values without the theme block.
  • Theme tokens work alongside $var template substitution (quickthumb render --var KEY=VALUE); $theme.* references are never treated as variables.

docs.title: Layer schemas
docs.text: The most common layers are shown below. Video, chart, QR code, counter, and plugin layers follow the same pattern; their fields are in the published schema and on their API reference pages.

docs.title: Background layer
docs.text:
{
  "type": "background",
  "color": "#0F172A",
  "gradient": null,
  "image": null,
  "opacity": 1.0,
  "blend_mode": null,
  "fit": null,
  "effects": []
}

Only include the fields you need; the rest use their defaults.

Gradient variants:

{
  "type": "background",
  "gradient": {
    "type": "linear",
    "angle": 120,
    "stops": [["#111827", 0.0], ["#11182700", 1.0]]
  }
}

{
  "type": "background",
  "gradient": {
    "type": "radial",
    "stops": [["#00000000", 0.0], ["#000000CC", 1.0]],
    "center": [0.5, 0.5]
  }
}

Image background:

{
  "type": "background",
  "image": "https://example.com/photo.jpg",
  "fit": "cover",
  "blend_mode": "multiply",
  "effects": [
    { "type": "filter", "blur": 4, "brightness": 0.75, "contrast": 1.1, "saturation": 0.9 }
  ]
}

docs.title: Text layer
docs.text:
{
  "type": "text",
  "content": "Hello World",
  "font_source": "auto",
  "font_variations": {},
  "emoji_style": "monochrome",
  "size": 72,
  "color": "#FFFFFF",
  "position": ["50%", "50%"],
  "align": "center",
  "max_height": null,
  "min_size": 1,
  "balance_lines": false,
  "opacity": 1.0,
  "rotation": 0.0,
  "effects": []
}

Rich text with TextPart list:

{
  "type": "text",
  "content": [
    {
      "text": "5 ",
      "color": "#FBBF24",
      "font_source": null,
      "font_variations": null,
      "emoji_style": null,
      "weight": 900,
      "effects": []
    },
    {
      "text": "WARNING SIGNS",
      "color": "#FFFFFF",
      "font_source": "auto",
      "font_variations": {},
      "emoji_style": "monochrome",
      "weight": 900,
      "effects": []
    }
  ],
  "size": 80,
  "position": ["8%", "55%"],
  "align": "left",
  "max_width": "65%",
  "auto_scale": false,
  "rotation": 0.0,
  "opacity": 1.0,
  "effects": [
    { "type": "stroke", "width": 3, "color": "#000000" },
    { "type": "shadow", "offset_x": 4, "offset_y": 4, "color": "#000000", "blur_radius": 8 }
  ]
}

Gradient-filled text:

{
  "type": "text",
  "content": "GRADIENT",
  "size": 120,
  "fill": {
    "type": "linear",
    "angle": 90,
    "stops": [["#FF6B6B", 0.0], ["#4ECDC4", 1.0]]
  },
  "position": ["50%", "50%"],
  "align": "center",
  "effects": []
}

Image-filled text:

{
  "type": "text",
  "content": "TEXTURE",
  "size": 140,
  "fill": {
    "type": "image",
    "path": "fire_texture.jpg",
    "fit": "cover"
  },
  "position": ["50%", "50%"],
  "align": "center",
  "effects": []
}

fill discriminator values: "linear", "radial", "image", the same tags as background gradients. fill can also be set per TextPart entry using the same discriminated object.

Align values: "center", "left", "right", "top-left", "top-center", "top-right", "bottom-left", "bottom-center", "bottom-right"

docs.title: Image layer
docs.text:
{
  "type": "image",
  "path": "portrait.png",
  "position": ["74%", "54%"],
  "width": 420,
  "height": 520,
  "fit": "cover",
  "align": "center",
  "opacity": 1.0,
  "rotation": 0.0,
  "remove_background": false,
  "border_radius": 24,
  "blend_mode": "normal",
  "effects": [
    { "type": "filter", "contrast": 1.1, "saturation": 1.05 },
    { "type": "shadow", "offset_x": 0, "offset_y": 12, "color": "#000000", "blur_radius": 24 }
  ]
}

docs.title: Shape layer
docs.text:
{
  "type": "shape",
  "shape": "rectangle",
  "position": [48, 48],
  "width": 320,
  "height": 96,
  "color": "#CC0000",
  "border_radius": 14,
  "opacity": 1.0,
  "rotation": 0.0,
  "align": "top-left",
  "effects": [
    { "type": "stroke", "width": 2, "color": "#FFFFFF" }
  ]
}

"shape" values: "rectangle", "ellipse", "pill", "triangle", "star", "polygon"

Star and polygon variants:

{
  "type": "shape",
  "shape": "star",
  "position": ["80%", "50%"],
  "width": 280,
  "height": 280,
  "color": "#7C5CFF",
  "align": "center",
  "rotation": 12,
  "star_points": 5,
  "inner_radius": 0.45
}

{
  "type": "shape",
  "shape": "polygon",
  "position": [600, 60],
  "width": 160,
  "height": 100,
  "color": "#53BF9D",
  "points": [[0.0, 0.25], [0.6, 0.25], [0.6, 0.0], [1.0, 0.5], [0.6, 1.0], [0.6, 0.75], [0.0, 0.75]]
}

points is required for "polygon" (and only valid there): at least 3 vertices, normalized 0.0–1.0 inside the shape box. star_points (≥ 3) and inner_radius (between 0 and 1, exclusive) only apply to "star".

docs.title: SVG layer
docs.text:
Rasterized at render time. Requires the quickthumb[svg] extra. See the SVG reference.

{
  "type": "svg",
  "path": "logo.svg",
  "position": ["92%", "10%"],
  "width": 120,
  "align": "center",
  "opacity": 1.0,
  "rotation": 0.0,
  "blend_mode": null,
  "effects": []
}

width/height set the raster size; aspect ratio is preserved when only one is given. SVG layers accept the same effects as image layers.

docs.title: Group layer
docs.text:
Auto-layout container: children are measured and stacked along a row or column, so they must not set position. See the Group reference.

{
  "type": "group",
  "direction": "column",
  "gap": 24,
  "padding": 0,
  "position": ["8%", "50%"],
  "align": ["left", "middle"],
  "item_align": "start",
  "children": [
    { "type": "shape", "shape": "pill", "width": 120, "height": 36, "color": "#E94560" },
    { "type": "text", "content": "AUTO LAYOUT", "size": 96, "color": "#FFFFFF", "weight": 900 },
    { "type": "text", "content": "No coordinates were harmed", "size": 40, "color": "#A2A8D3" }
  ]
}
  • direction: "column" (default) or "row"
  • gap: pixels between children; padding: int, [vertical, horizontal], or [top, right, bottom, left]
  • item_align: cross-axis placement, one of "start", "center", or "end"
  • children types: "text", "image", "shape", "svg", or nested "group"

docs.title: Outline layer
docs.text:
{
  "type": "outline",
  "width": 12,
  "color": "#B8FF00",
  "offset": 0,
  "opacity": 1.0
}

docs.title: Effect schemas
docs.text:
Effects are embedded in each layer's "effects" array and use a "type" discriminator:

StrokeShadowGlowFilterBackground (text)GrainDuotoneInner shadowBackdrop blur 
{ "type": "stroke", "width": 4, "color": "#000000" }

{ "type": "shadow", "offset_x": 4, "offset_y": 8, "color": "#000000", "blur_radius": 12 }

{ "type": "glow", "color": "#B8FF00", "radius": 16, "opacity": 0.35 }

{ "type": "filter", "blur": 4, "brightness": 0.75, "contrast": 1.1, "saturation": 0.9 }

{ "type": "background", "color": "#111827CC", "padding": [16, 24], "border_radius": 14, "opacity": 1.0 }

{ "type": "grain", "intensity": 0.12, "monochrome": true, "blend_mode": "overlay", "opacity": 1.0 }

blend_mode values: "overlay", "screen", "multiply", "normal". Optional "seed" integer for deterministic output.

{ "type": "duotone", "shadows": "#0A1730", "highlights": "#7FADFF", "opacity": 1.0 }

{ "type": "inner_shadow", "offset_x": 0, "offset_y": 6, "color": "#00000080", "blur_radius": 12, "opacity": 1.0 }

{ "type": "backdrop_blur", "radius": 24, "opacity": 1.0 }

Which effects each layer accepts is listed in the Effects reference.

docs.text:
A full YouTube-style thumbnail spec:

{

  "width": 1280,
  "height": 720,
  "layers": [
    {
      "type": "background",
      "image": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f85e504b3",

    },
    {

    },

docs.title: Generating specs with an LLM
docs.text: The AI Workflow recipe covers this end to end: giving the model the published schema, sending validation errors and diagnose() findings back to it, and asking for edits instead of new designs.

docs.title: Serialization notes
docs.text: Field Serialized form align String: "center", "top-left", etc. blend_mode String: "multiply", "normal", etc. fit String: "cover", "contain", "fill" position JSON array: [640, 360] or ["50%", "50%"] Gradient stops JSON array of ["#color", 0.0] pairs null fields Omitted fields default to null / their default value theme block Resolved at parse time; to_json() emits resolved values without the theme block

docs.title: Choose an output format
docs.text:
Use the same Canvas or Deck to create images, presentations, and animation. Choose a format for where you want to use the result:

I want to… Choose What you need Publish an image PNG, JPEG, or WebP The base package Share a presentation in a browser HTML The base package Edit slides in PowerPoint or Keynote PPTX The pptx extra Share a document PDF The pdf extra Share a short animation GIF The base package Publish a video MP4, WebM, or MOV FFmpeg; MOV also needs the prores_ks encoder Use vector artwork SVG or Lottie SVG uses the base package. Lottie supports a limited Canvas-only subset.

docs.title: Export an image
docs.text:
The file extension selects the format. This example needs Python 3.11+ and pip install quickthumb:

from quickthumb import Canvas

canvas = Canvas(1280, 720).background(color="#155BD7").text(
    "Make an idea visible.", size=72, color="#FFFFFF", position=(80, 300)
)
result = canvas.export("image.png")
print(result.written_paths)

Open image.png in the working directory. Exporting again replaces the file. Use .jpg or .webp for those formats. A Deck exported to an image format writes numbered slide files; written_paths tells you their names.

docs.title: Make slides or animation
docs.text:
Follow the presentation and video examples for a runnable image, two-slide HTML presentation, and GIF. For PowerPoint or PDF, install the relevant optional extra first. MP4 and WebM require FFmpeg installed separately.

Formats do not preserve every effect or animation in the same way. PowerPoint and PDF may use image fallbacks, and an HTML presentation does not play Deck narration. Check the result in the app where you plan to use it.

For format support, export receipts, advanced options, and fallbacks, see the export reference.

docs.title: Animation timing
docs.text: Set animation and slide durations in seconds. Export a GIF for a silent loop, video for motion with sound, or HTML for an interactive presentation.

docs.title: Animate and hold a scene
docs.text:
This example fades in a shape over one second, then holds the final image for two seconds. It writes timed.gif in the working directory, replacing any existing file with that name:

from quickthumb import AnimationSpec, Canvas, GifOptions

canvas = Canvas(320, 180).background(color="#102030").shape(
    "rectangle", (80, 40), 160, 100, "#42CEB7",
    animation=AnimationSpec.fade(duration=1),
)
canvas.export("timed.gif", animation=GifOptions(hold=2))

Use VideoOptions(hold=2) for MP4, WebM, or MOV. Video export requires FFmpeg. GifOptions and VideoOptions also accept fps; their defaults are 20 and 30 respectively. GIF has no audio. See output formats for setup.

docs.title: Slide duration and transitions
docs.text:
A Deck plays each slide's motion and incoming transition, then holds the settled slide for hold seconds (three by default). Later slides use a 0.5-second crossfade unless you choose another transition; Cut() switches immediately.

For Deck video, slide(duration=...) sets the slide's total window, including its incoming transition and animation. Narration can set the window when no explicit duration is supplied. A longer visual animation is allowed to finish; narration is trimmed or padded to its scheduled window. GIF ignores slide narration and slide(duration=...).

advance_after on a transition replaces the usual hold; the slide still waits for its animation and any video narration or explicit duration to finish. For precise boundary rules, see the timing reference.

docs.title: Audio, captions and reduced motion
docs.text:
MP4, WebM, and MOV can include supported clip audio, slide narration, and a soundtrack. GIF is silent. Video clip captions use times relative to the placed clip and are burned into supported video frames.

With ExportPolicy(reduced_motion=True), authored layer motion and transitions are suppressed while holds, narration, and caption timing remain. Default Deck crossfades can remain. HTML presentations keep interactive click cues, but do not play Deck narration and show video layers as static frames. Check your export in the destination app.

docs.title: Temporal exposure
docs.text:
To add motion blur to GIF, video, or an image sequence, pass MotionBlur to the corresponding export options:

from quickthumb import MotionBlur, VideoOptions

canvas.export(
    "exposure.mp4",
    animation=VideoOptions(fps=30, motion_blur=MotionBlur(samples=8, shutter_angle=180)),
)

Motion blur is an export setting; HTML and PowerPoint do not reproduce it. MotionBlur accepts 2–64 samples and a shutter angle greater than 0 and at most 360 degrees. See the motion blur reference for timing, support, and export receipts.

docs.title: Support and receipts
docs.text: Use result.capability_report after export to inspect applied motion blur and result.timing_metrics for encoded playback. See the support table.

docs.title: Choose the clock
docs.text: sample() observes the authored timeline; an encoded GIF or video can have a slightly different duration or frame count because of its format. HTML is interactive rather than a fixed-duration video. See the sampling and timing reference when exact frame times or export metrics matter.

docs.title: Verify playback
docs.text: Play the exported file and check slide changes, captions, sound, and the final hold in the app where it will be shared. For exact timing, inspect result.timing_metrics; the timing reference also describes the project's playback tests.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Use Canvas to author a scene and Deck to sequence scenes. Both implement the same document operations; individual layer pages describe their authoring fields.

docs.title: Supported public surface
docs.text:
Import documented authoring types and result models from quickthumb, and audio analysis from the documented quickthumb.audio module. A name being importable from another module does not make it a supported entry point.

Surface Supported use Authoring Canvas, Deck, documented layer/effect models, motion tracks, transitions and option models Document operations validate(), inspect(), diagnose(), prefetch_assets(), sample() and export() on either document kind; inspect_document() for generic consumers Results Typed reports, ExportResult, CanonicalFrame / FrameSequence, and ImageSequence* results; serialize them with model_dump_json() JSON to_json(), Canvas.from_json(), Deck.from_json(), canvas_json_schema() and document_json_schema() Audio authoring quickthumb.audio.analyze_audio() and AudioAnalysis; bake source-clock onset times and RMS-driven scale into numeric motion Specialist output Documented render(), render_frame(), to_*() and export_image_sequence() methods when their return type or controls fit the task

export() is the recommended file boundary: it preflights capability policy and returns written paths and diagnostics. Specialist methods have their own return values and do not all enforce that policy; see output API. Keep format-specific options at that boundary rather than calling exporters directly.

Modules beginning with _, renderer/context objects, and timeline compilation helpers are implementation details. They can change or disappear without a supported lifecycle. Use sample() to consume frames instead of coordinating a compiler and renderer. The reference pages and generated schema describe the installed version's supported fields; public does not mean frozen across versions.

docs.title: One document workflow
docs.text:
This uses the same layer data in Python, canonical JSON and a Deck, with no renderer objects or optional dependencies:

from quickthumb import Canvas, Deck, Document, ExportResult

canvas = Canvas(320, 180).background(color="#102030").shape(
    "rectangle", position=(24, 24), width=80, height=40, color="#42CEB7",
    id="badge", motion_key="brand", anchor=(0, 0),
)
restored = Canvas.from_json(canvas.to_json())
document: Document = Deck(slides=[restored])
result: ExportResult = document.export("slides.png")
print(result.written_paths)  # Numbered paths are reported by the result.
print(document.sample().frames[0].sha256)

docs.title: Shared layer vocabulary
docs.text:
Canvas layers use the same fields when carried by a Deck slide or canonical JSON. A Deck adds slide order, transitions, narration and notes; it does not rename layer fields. Python tuples become JSON arrays, enum values become strings, and each layer has a type discriminator.

Field or concept Meaning id Optional identifier unique within a Canvas scene, including group descendants. Each Deck slide has its own identity scope. motion_key Optional matching key across scenes for Morph transitions; distinct from a scene-local id. position, width, height Authored placement and size, in pixels or percentage strings where the layer accepts them. Percentages resolve against the canvas; consult the layer reference for required fields and sizing rules. align The point of a layer's layout box placed at position; also controls text alignment. See Align. rotation, anchor Rotation is in degrees. anchor=(x, y) is a normalized 0–1 pivot for canonical motion, distinct from layout alignment. Static rotation has its own framing; see transform anchors. opacity Layer opacity from 0 to 1 where supported. animation A preset or AnimationSpec containing typed tracks and timing. Position tracks are offsets from authored placement; scale tracks transform the outer object, while ImageZoomTrack changes image content inside its frame. Group Auto-layout owns child placement. Use .group() for rows/columns rather than positioning each child. parent / null Advanced, scene-local transform hierarchy for top-level animatable layers. Child placement is parent-local; percentage coordinates still resolve against the canvas. This is separate from group layout. See parent transforms.

Not every layer accepts every field: backgrounds, outlines, nulls and drawable layers have different roles. Their reference pages and the JSON schema are the field-level contract. Plugin registrations declare parameters and can supply rendering callbacks through an explicit PluginRegistry; parsing JSON does not package or install those callbacks.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What it covers Canvas Creating a canvas, every layer method, checks, and export methods Deck Several canvases as one PDF, PPTX, HTML slideshow, video, or image sequence Document inspection inspect_document() and generic Canvas/Deck sampling consumers Background .background(): colors, gradients, and images Text .text() and TextPart: text and rich text Image .image(): placed images and cut-outs Shape .shape(): rectangles, ellipses, pills, triangles, stars, polygons Path .path(): filled/stroked SVG path data and bounded motion SVG .svg(): icons and logos from SVG files Video .video(): video clips, captions, and audio Group .group(): auto-layout rows and columns Outline .outline(): a border around the canvas Data visualizations .chart() and .qr_code() Effects Stroke, Shadow, Glow, Filter, Background, Grain, Duotone, InnerShadow, BackdropBlur Enums & Gradients Align, BlendMode, FitMode, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, TextFillImage

docs.title: Error types
docs.text: Exception When raised ValidationError Invalid arguments passed to a layer builder (raised immediately) RenderingError Failure during .render(), .to_base64(), or .to_data_url()

docs.title: Audio-reactive authoring
docs.text:
quickthumb.audio.analyze_audio(path, cache_dir=None) analyzes a local audio source ahead of authoring; it requires FFmpeg. It returns a validated AudioAnalysis record with transient onset times and source-relative RMS amplitudes. Onsets identify sharp increases in loudness; they are not a musical beat grid or a tempo estimate.

Use an onset as an ordinary numeric TimingSpec.start. This avoids a dependency on soundtrack options when sampling, restoring JSON, or rendering in workers:

from quickthumb import AnimationSpec, ColorTrack, KeyframeSpec, TimingSpec
from quickthumb.audio import analyze_audio

analysis = analyze_audio("music.wav")
if analysis.onsets:
    motion = AnimationSpec.timeline(
        ColorTrack(keyframes=[
            KeyframeSpec(time=0, value="#102030"),
            KeyframeSpec(time=0.2, value="#42CEB7"),
        ]),
        timing=TimingSpec(start=analysis.onsets[0], duration=0.2),
        easing="linear",
    )

Attach motion to a layer's animation=. See the runnable examples/audio_onsets.py for a scene, analysis sidecar, canonical JSON and MP4 with the same source as its soundtrack. The numeric motion is also inspectable with inspect_motion() and uses each target's existing color-track support or declared fallback. HTML presentation does not play the soundtrack; GIF remains silent. Baked timing is not a claim of live audio synchronization in either format.

docs.title: Source clock and RMS
docs.text:
All times are seconds from the beginning of the first decoded audio stream. Values describe source amplitude; silence has zero RMS and no onsets. Check onsets before indexing because a track can have none.

Analysis resolution and onset detection

Analysis uses mono audio resampled to 8 kHz and contiguous 160-sample (20 ms) windows. rms[i] is the linear RMS amplitude of the window starting at i * 0.02; the final window may be shorter. Values are source amplitudes, not normalized per track. Silence has zero RMS and no onsets.

The versioned detector requires an RMS attack above 0.01 and twice both the previous window and the mean of the previous ten windows, with at least 100 ms between anchors. Reference transients are tested within one 20 ms window; gradual attacks and musical offbeats need not produce anchors. An onset index can be absent: check onsets before indexing.

Export gain, soundtrack looping/fade-out, narration and other mixed audio do not change this source analysis. Deck timing is slide-local: authors must translate a soundtrack onset into the intended slide's clock. Nothing automatically repeats or relocates anchors when export options change.

docs.title: Loudness-driven scale
docs.text:
AudioAnalysis.scale_track(min_scale=1.0, max_scale=1.15) returns an ordinary ScaleTrack. Attach it to AnimationSpec.timeline(); no soundtrack or analyzer is consulted while converting stored RMS into motion:

pulse = AnimationSpec.timeline(
    analysis.scale_track(min_scale=1.0, max_scale=1.4)
)

The helper divides each RMS amplitude by the loudest window in this analysis, then maps that ratio into the requested scale range. Silence maps to min_scale, the peak maps to max_scale, and an entirely silent analysis stays at min_scale. This is source-relative normalization: a quiet recording can produce the same response as a louder copy, and export volume does not affect it. Both bounds must be finite positive numbers with max_scale >= min_scale.

Each keyframe holds its value over its 20 ms window, including a shorter final window; there is no interpolation before an attack. At the exact source end an additional keyframe returns to min_scale, so settled holds and subsequent slides do not retain a loud final pulse. The inferred animation duration equals analysis.duration. An explicit TimingSpec must allow that full duration; setting start shifts the entire source clock rather than trimming it.

The generated track is regular canonical JSON: sample(), inspect_motion(), workers and exporters consume it through the existing scale-track path. Reduced motion suppresses this track and keeps the authored static geometry. HTML/PPTX follow their declared scale support, but do not acquire live soundtrack playback or synchronization. The runnable example combines an onset-triggered color change and a loudness-driven scale pulse with source audio in MP4.

docs.title: Store and reuse
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from quickthumb.audio import AudioAnalysis

Path("analysis.json").write_text(analysis.model_dump_json(), encoding="utf-8")
stored = AudioAnalysis.model_validate_json(Path("analysis.json").read_text())

The record includes its schema/algorithm version, source SHA-256, FFmpeg version, sampling parameters, duration, ordered onsets and RMS windows. Its JSON schema is available through AudioAnalysis.model_json_schema(). A sidecar and motion baked into document JSON can be loaded and sampled without the source audio or FFmpeg. Exporting audio still requires its source and the usual media tools.

analyze_audio itself requires FFmpeg (QUICKTHUMB_FFMPEG overrides the binary). It caches records under the system temporary directory's quickthumb-audio folder, or the supplied cache_dir, using source bytes, algorithm, fixed parameters and FFmpeg version as the identity. Cache writes are atomic. Changing source bytes or decoder/algorithm versions creates a new entry; a corrupt entry raises an error identifying the file to remove. Keep a sidecar to pin authoring results across decoder upgrades rather than relying on an evictable cache.

Inputs are bounded to 64 MiB and ten minutes of decoded audio. Analysis has a 60-second timeout. Missing/non-audio files, unsupported FFmpeg filters and exceeded limits fail with actionable errors; analysis is never silently truncated. These limits bound authoring work, not rendering duration.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: .background() adds a full-canvas background layer. Multiple background calls stack in render order; the first call is at the back.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
canvas.background(
    color=None,
    gradient=None,
    image=None,
    opacity=1.0,
    blend_mode=None,
    fit=None,
    effects=None,
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description color str \| tuple \| None None Solid fill color. Hex string ("#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA") or RGB/RGBA tuple. gradient LinearGradient \| RadialGradient \| None None Gradient fill. See Enums & Gradients. image str \| None None Local file path or remote URL. opacity float 1.0 Layer opacity from 0.0 (transparent) to 1.0 (opaque). blend_mode str \| BlendMode \| None None How this layer composites over previous layers. See BlendMode. fit str \| FitMode \| None None How an image fills the canvas. See FitMode. effects list \| None [] Background effects. Accepts Filter and Grain.

docs.title: Solid color
docs.text: canvas.background(color="#0F172A")

docs.title: Gradient overlay
docs.text:
from quickthumb import LinearGradient

canvas.background(
    gradient=LinearGradient(
        angle=120,
        stops=[("#111827", 0.0), ("#11182700", 1.0)],
    ),
    opacity=0.7,
)

docs.title: Remote image with effects
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Filter

canvas.background(
    image="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1516321318423-f06f85e504b3",
    fit="cover",
    blend_mode="multiply",
    effects=[Filter(blur=4, brightness=0.75, contrast=1.1, saturation=0.9)],
)

docs.title: Dark overlay
docs.text: canvas.background(color="#000000", opacity=0.4)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Background layers always cover the entire canvas.
  • color, gradient, and image can each be used independently or together within one layer.
  • blend_mode applies when compositing this layer over previous layers.
  • Supports both local file paths and remote URLs for image.
  • For available effects, see Filter and Grain.

docs.title: Canvas
docs.text: The Canvas is the root object. It holds dimensions and an ordered list of layers. Its authoring fields follow the shared layer vocabulary, which also applies to Deck slides and canonical JSON.

docs.title: Canvas(width=None, height=None)
docs.text:
from quickthumb import Canvas

canvas = Canvas(1280, 720)
Parameter Type Description width int \| None Canvas width in pixels. Must be a positive integer. height int \| None Canvas height in pixels. Must be a positive integer.

Width and height must be given together or both omitted. A canvas built without a size (Canvas()) is unsized: it accepts layer builders but cannot be rendered, diagnosed, or serialized until it gets a size, either directly or by being added to a sized Deck, which gives it the deck's default size. Check canvas.has_size to tell the difference.

docs.title: Canvas.from_aspect_ratio(ratio, base_width)
docs.text:
Creates a canvas from an aspect ratio string and a base width. Height is calculated automatically.

wide     = Canvas.from_aspect_ratio("16:9", base_width=1280)   # 1280×720
square   = Canvas.from_aspect_ratio("1:1",  base_width=1080)   # 1080×1080
vertical = Canvas.from_aspect_ratio("9:16", base_width=1080)   # 1080×1920
Parameter Type Description ratio str Aspect ratio string in "W:H" format, e.g. "16:9" base_width int Canvas width in pixels

docs.title: Layer builders
docs.text:
All builder methods mutate the canvas and return self, enabling method chaining.

Method Description .background(...) Add a full-canvas background layer .text(...) Add a text layer .image(...) Add an overlay image layer .shape(...) Add a shape layer .path(...) Draw a filled or stroked path .svg(...) Add an SVG layer, rasterized at render time .video(...) Add a video clip to an animated composition .counter(...) Add an animated number .group(...) Add an auto-layout group of child layers .outline(...) Add a canvas border .chart(...) Add a deterministic bar or line chart layer from a typed chart spec .qr_code(...) Add a square QR code layer .custom(fn) Add a Pillow callback layer

See the data visualization reference and the other individual reference pages for full parameter details.

docs.title: Animated counters
docs.text:
