Need Entry point Write a file with capability policy and a result receipt export(path, ...) Draw debug boxes or use the lower-level file renderer render(path, ...) Get bytes or an in-memory document to_mp4(), to_gif(), to_html(), etc. Export narrated Deck slides export(path, animation=VideoOptions(hold=3)) / to_mp4(hold=3) Write silent animation frames plus a manifest export_image_sequence(directory, options=...) Write bounded Canvas-only Lottie vectors canvas.export("scene.lot", animation=LottieOptions(fps=30, hold=3)); see Lottie vectors

All animated byte methods and options use hold for settled-state seconds. render_quality="standard" or "high" controls animation compositing; quality on export()/render() controls compression: JPEG accepts integer values 1–95 and WebP accepts 1–100. Keep workers=1 unless advanced spawn-based rendering is needed. Optional temporal exposure adds motion blur to Canvas exports. Both export() and render() enforce file capability policies such as unsupported_motion="error" before writing; export() also returns the receipt. Byte methods expose target-specific controls without the shared file receipt. Use the returned written_paths for Deck raster sequences: they are numbered files. Image sequences keep a separate API because their destination is a new directory.

docs.title: Format and option selection
docs.text:
Canvas and Deck use the same selection rules except that .lot is Canvas-only; Deck rejects Lottie output.

Input Result File extension, with no format Selects the output; .jpg/.jpeg report output_format="jpeg", .htm/.html report "html". format="PNG", "JPEG" or "WEBP" (case-insensitive) Selects raster encoding for a raster, unknown or extensionless filename. The requested filename is kept; it is not renamed to match the encoding. Raster format with a document or animated extension Rejected rather than writing image bytes into an SVG, PDF, HTML, PPTX, video or .lot filename. quality JPEG integer 1–95 or WebP integer 1–100; rejected for other targets. animation GifOptions for GIF; VideoOptions for MP4/WebM/MOV; LottieOptions for Canvas .lot. Rejected for other static/document targets.

Format selection, compression quality and animation option-family conflicts are rejected before asset reads or file writes. Codec-specific limits are validated during export preparation. Rendering or encoding failures can still occur later; ordinary file exports are not an atomic multi-file transaction. Inspect written_paths rather than guessing Canvas or numbered Deck filenames. A Deck cannot be written as a single SVG; export its Canvas slides individually. See image sequences for their separate new-directory and encoding-option contract.

docs.title: Document layer routing
docs.text:
Canvas and Deck HTML/PPTX exports, and Canvas SVG/PDF exports, report executed layer routes in result.capability_report with feature="layer_representation". Native HTML/CSS, SVG/PDF primitives, editable PowerPoint objects and original embedded SVG have support="native"; emitted PNG fragments have support="fallback" and fallback="rasterize". PPTX content combining an editable foreground with a fixed glow image has support="partial" and fallback="rasterize"; re-export after foreground edits to update that effect. These are representation observations, not pixel-fidelity measurements.

result.fallback_diagnostics identifies the affected inspection layer_id and reason. A retained group includes its descendant IDs in layer_ids; a shared backdrop-dependent prefix has no single layer_id and lists all contributing sources in layer_ids. Such composites are reported together because their appearance depends on the combined pixels. Flattened auto-layout children keep their original inspection IDs. Empty raster fragments and empty text produce no element and no representation observation.

For these executed routes, native_attempt=True includes native content emission or execution/verification of a native candidate that falls back to raster. Read support and fallback to identify the representation actually adopted. False means raster capture was selected before native generation or verification. Capability-only diagnostics can leave this fact unknown (None). Parent scenes report their static composite in SVG/PDF/PPTX; HTML can also report PNG sources with baked affine CSS motion. Existing motion capability diagnostics remain separate. SVG/PDF observations describe authored-static output. PDF text retains embedded fonts when supported; shaping, glyph coverage and font-embedding constraints can instead select an explained raster fragment.

Executed Deck observations also carry a zero-based slide_index. Layer IDs stay local to each slide, matching deck.inspect().slides[index]; use both fields to distinguish repeated IDs between slides. Canvas observations omit slide_index. Deck HTML keeps its interactive cues, transitions and notes; these representation records do not turn a click-driven slideshow into fixed-duration playback.

For example, ExportPolicy(unsupported_motion="error") does not reject a static masked shape: this HTML route preserves its mask using a PNG fragment and reports that decision. No layer-selection policy is added. This executed routing report covers Canvas SVG/PDF and Canvas/Deck HTML/PPTX; Deck PDF does not yet collect these observations. Fidelity metrics describe the complete document and are not attributed to individual fallback layers. Rendering all slides precedes opening the HTML destination, so an unsupported later slide or strict motion rejection preserves an existing file.

PPTX routes describe the actual OOXML representation: native text boxes and autoshapes remain editable objects; PNG fragments preserve their raster payload and placement but lose per-glyph/vector editing. Raster reasons include masks, backdrop compositing, image/radial text fills and unsupported font semantics. Canvas observations omit a slide index; Deck observations identify their slide. PPTX file exports build the complete presentation before opening the destination, so a later source-rendering failure preserves an existing file.

These structural observations do not certify a PowerPoint or Keynote pixel match, font availability, animation timing or transparency in a particular viewer. There is no PPTX fidelity policy or automatic application renderer. PPTX geometry uses 9,525 EMU per source pixel (96 pixels per inch), or 0.75 PDF points per source pixel. A later PDF-based viewer comparison must derive scale from its actual page dimensions rather than assuming the PDF exporter's one-point-per-pixel mapping.

docs.title: Migrating output calls
docs.text:
• Deck.to_mp4() now plays animation, matching Canvas and file exports. Replace old to_animated_mp4() and to_narrated_mp4() calls with to_mp4().
  • Replace render_mp4() and render_narrated_mp4() with export("deck.mp4"). The separate still-slide encoder is removed, with no aliases. To retain still scenes, author static canvases and use Cut(); this does not freeze an already animated Deck or promise identical encoded output.
  • export_image_sequence() replaces export_png_sequence(); the public options/manifest/result models are now ImageSequence*, with no obsolete aliases.
  • Replace animated Deck slide_duration= and narrated default_duration= with hold=. Replace animation quality= with render_quality=, including saved GifOptions, VideoOptions and ImageSequenceOptions JSON. There are no aliases.

docs.title: How export works
docs.text:
SVG, PDF and PPTX exporters keep eligible layers native and use canonical PNG fragments where a native representation is unavailable. Positions, wrapping and alignment share the raster renderer's layout math. HTML uses the same native-or-raster approach; see HTML below.

Lottie instead accepts a bounded native-vector subset and rejects unsupported content before writing. It never substitutes PNG frames.

Layer SVG PPTX PDF Background color / gradient Native rect + gradient defs Native shape fill (linear gradients native, radial embedded) Native fill; opaque gradients native, translucent gradients embedded Outline Native rect stroke Native bordered rectangle Native rectangle stroke Shapes (all primitives) Native elements, incl. rotation and stroke/shadow/glow Native autoshapes; polygons become freeforms Native paths incl. rotation; shapes with effects embedded Text (simple & rich) Native <text> per line/run, incl. wrapping, letter spacing, gradient fills, effects Editable text boxes with per-run styling Native selectable text when its font can be embedded and the text does not need complex shaping; unsupported fonts and gradient/image fills or blur effects are embedded as pixels Groups (auto-layout) Children exported natively at their layout positions Same Same Images & image-filled text Embedded PNG fragment Embedded picture Embedded picture SVG layers Embedded as vector data URL (raster when effects are applied) Embedded picture Embedded picture Blend modes & custom layers Everything below the last blend/custom layer is flattened into one PNG Same Same

docs.title: Decks (multiple images and slides)
docs.text:
A Deck is an ordered list of canvases. Each slide is a full Canvas and renders exactly as it would on its own. See the Deck API reference for the full method list.

Give the deck a size once and each slide can be a bare Canvas() that inherits it:

from quickthumb import AudioTrack, Canvas, Deck, VideoOptions

deck = (
    Deck(1280, 720)   # default slide size; Deck.from_aspect_ratio("16:9", 1280) also works
    .slide(Canvas().background(color="#101820").text(content="Cover", size=96, color="#FFFFFF"))
    .slide(Canvas().background(color="#1A1A2E").text(content="Body", size=64, color="#FFFFFF"))
)
# pre-built canvases work too: Deck(slides=[cover, body])

deck.render("deck.pdf")     # one multi-page PDF (a page per slide)
deck.render("deck.pptx")    # one multi-slide PPTX (a slide per slide)
deck.render("deck.gif")     # one animation playing transitions between slides
deck.export("deck.mp4")     # animated slides with per-slide narration
deck.render(
    "deck.mp4",
    animation=VideoOptions(soundtrack=AudioTrack(path="music.mp3", loop=True)),
)  # animated + mixed audio
deck.render("animated.mp4", animation=VideoOptions(fps=20))  # animated, silent
deck.render("slides.png")   # numbered sequence: slides_01.png, slides_02.png, …

pdf_bytes = deck.to_pdf()
pptx_bytes = deck.to_pptx()
gif_bytes = deck.to_gif()
webm_bytes = deck.to_webm()
mp4_bytes = deck.to_mp4()   # timeline with per-slide narration

render() dispatches on the output extension: .pdf and .pptx produce a single document; .gif, .mp4, .webm, and .mov produce an animation; and raster extensions have no native multi-page container, so the deck writes one file per slide as a zero-padded numbered sequence and returns the written paths.

Slides may have different dimensions. deck.diagnose() aggregates each slide's diagnostics (each tagged with its slide_index) and adds a mixed-slide-size warning when they differ. The PDF path sizes each page to its slide, but PPTX has a single presentation size taken from the first slide, so slides larger than the first are clipped by PowerPoint. Keep slides the same size when targeting .pptx. Decks round-trip through JSON with deck.to_json() / Deck.from_json(...), reusing the per-canvas serialization.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The CLI picks the format from the output extension too:

quickthumb render spec.json -o card.svg
quickthumb render spec.json -o card.pptx
quickthumb render spec.json -o card.pdf

# Live HTML slides; open /?presenter for the presenter dashboard
quickthumb serve slides.py

docs.title: Transparent video
docs.text: Export reference · Choose an output format

docs.title: Transparent WebM
docs.text:
VP9 WebM can preserve alpha through VideoOptions(transparent=True), or the keyword-only transparent=True argument to Canvas.to_webm() and Deck.to_webm(). The default is False; existing opaque exports keep their matte and encoder settings. This is an export option, not a layer or motion property, so it is absent from Canvas/Deck JSON and inspect_motion(); VideoOptions.model_validate_json() and its model JSON schema expose the strict boolean option. validate_export() continues to describe document motion, while render() rejects transparent options on unsupported output formats.

canvas.render("overlay.webm", animation=VideoOptions(transparent=True))
deck.render("overlay.webm", animation=VideoOptions(transparent=True, render_quality="high", workers=2))
webm_bytes = canvas.to_webm(transparent=True)
options = VideoOptions.model_validate_json('{"transparent": true, "fps": 24}')

Only the export matte is skipped. Authored backgrounds remain visible, empty areas and mixed-size slide letterboxing stay transparent, and a transition on slide zero starts from transparency. Fade and mask transitions interpolate premultiplied colors; covering and scaled slides composite with source-over alpha. Keyed Morph normalizes mixed-size slides to the first slide's output space before interpolating positions, dimensions and translucent pixels. The existing parent/caption Morph fallback restrictions still apply.

Both compositing quality modes, spawn workers, soundtracks and Deck narration work with transparent WebM. The encoder streams RGBA into VP9 yuva420p with lossless VP9 coding to protect the alpha plane. The RGBA-to-YUV conversion can change decoded alpha by one 8-bit level; RGB remains chroma-subsampled (4:2:0), so source color pixels are not lossless. Files can be larger than opaque WebM. The existing bounded frame batches and atomic destination replacement remain. Transparent transitions use temporary floating-point planes for accurate premultiplied blending; memory usage grows with frame size and worker count. MP4, GIF, and document/raster output reject this video option before writing the destination. PNG animation sequences use the separate export_image_sequence() API.

Use a player or editor that supports VP9 WebM alpha. To inspect the actual alpha plane with FFmpeg, select the libvpx decoder before the input:

ffmpeg -c:v libvpx-vp9 -i overlay.webm -frames:v 1 -pix_fmt rgba frame.png

The native VP9 decoder may report/decode only color; alpha_mode metadata alone is not proof of preserved transparency. The regression tests decode RGBA with libvpx and compare transparent, translucent and opaque pixels. See examples/transparent_lower_third.py for an overlay with an authored translucent panel and transparent surroundings.

docs.title: ProRes 4444 MOV
docs.text:
Canvas and Deck can export .mov with the fixed ProRes 4444 profile, using FFmpeg's prores_ks encoder. MOV always plays the animated timeline, including Deck transitions and narration. transparent is the same strict boolean option as WebM and defaults to False: ordinary MOV composites onto the matte; opt-in alpha skips only that matte. Authored backgrounds, letterboxing, transitions, quality modes and workers follow the transparent WebM behavior above.

canvas.render("overlay.mov", animation=VideoOptions(transparent=True, fps=24))
deck.export("overlay.mov", animation=VideoOptions(transparent=True, render_quality="high", workers=2))
mov_bytes = canvas.to_mov(hold=2.0, transparent=True)
mov_bytes = deck.to_mov(hold=2.0, transparent=True, soundtrack="music.wav")

MOV retains exact canvas dimensions without cropping odd-width or odd-height frames. It encodes 4:4:4 chroma with 16-bit alpha coding (yuva444p10le) for transparent output, delivering industry-standard alpha fidelity for professional video editing tools such as Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and Adobe Premiere.

Soundtracks, per-slide narration and embedded video audio are encoded as AAC, using the same scheduling, looping, padding and trimming rules as animated MP4. A Canvas MOV with no audio inputs contains only video. Deck MOV retains the existing narration workflow’s silent AAC bed even when no slides have narration. The fixed codec/profile and audio choices have no selection API. ProRes files can be substantially larger than WebM/MP4, and require a ProRes-capable player or editor. Encoded segments stay bounded and destinations are replaced only after the full encode and mux succeed. A missing prores_ks encoder raises a rendering error and preserves any existing destination. Decode pixels, rather than relying on profile metadata, to check alpha:

ffmpeg -i overlay.mov -frames:v 1 -pix_fmt rgba frame.png

examples/transparent_lower_third.py writes both WebM and ProRes MOV overlays.

docs.title: Format fidelity and validation
docs.text: Export reference · Choose an output format

docs.title: Optional static SVG fidelity report
docs.text:
Request a CairoSVG comparison through ExportPolicy when the current job has explicit acceptance limits. All three limits are required; there are no built-in format budgets. This example requests exact visible RGBA rather than an application-specific allowance for edge or font differences:

from quickthumb import Canvas, ExportPolicy

policy = ExportPolicy(fidelity={"svg": {
    "pixel_tolerance": 0,
    "max_different_pixel_ratio": 0,
    "min_hash_similarity": 1,
}})
canvas = Canvas(160, 90).background(color="#123456")
result = canvas.export("checked.svg", policy=policy)
comparison = result.pixel_metrics.fidelity
print(comparison.verdict, comparison.pixel_diff_ratio, comparison.hash_similarity)

The optional quickthumb[svg] extra and system Cairo are needed only when the selected SVG export requests this check. The report records CairoSVG/Cairo versions, the canonical render environment, applied limits and actual rasterized dimensions. It compares the authored-static sample() still, with no resize. exact means all visible RGBA channels match; tolerated satisfies the supplied pixel-ratio and average-hash limits; out_of_policy fails a limit or dimensions. Mean absolute error is normalized over four channels, and the maximum channel delta is also reported. Fully transparent pixels ignore hidden RGB, so this definition of exact is distinct from canonical raw-pixel SHA-256 equality. The 8×8 average hash composites onto white; RGBA measurements independently catch alpha loss even when that hash is identical.

This is report-only: the original SVG representation is written even when the verdict is out_of_policy. A fidelity diagnostic describes the observation; no new raster fallback is selected. Missing/failed reference rendering raises before the destination is opened, preserving an existing file. Default exports and non-SVG targets do not perform this comparison.

The observation applies to static Cairo rendering in the recorded environment. Cairo uses installed fonts and does not honor embedded CSS @font-face, so the same font environment must be available separately; see the CairoSVG documentation. It is not a browser, HTML, or animation fidelity guarantee. SVG keeps its existing authored-static motion behavior.

docs.title: Optional static PDF fidelity report
docs.text:
Canvas PDF exports accept the same three explicit limits under the "pdf" key:

policy = ExportPolicy(fidelity={"pdf": {
    "pixel_tolerance": 0,
    "max_different_pixel_ratio": 0,
    "min_hash_similarity": 1,
}})
result = Canvas(160, 90).background(color="#123456").export("checked.pdf", policy=policy)
print(result.pixel_metrics.fidelity.verdict)

Install quickthumb[pdf] for ReportLab and the optional PDFium observer. Default PDF exports do not import PDFium. Requested comparison renders the actual PDF bytes on transparent RGBA at scale 1: this exporter uses one PDF point per canonical pixel, not a 96-DPI print-size conversion. The report records PDFium and binding versions, actual page size in points, page count, rendered dimensions and the canonical environment. Native PDFium document/render/cleanup calls are serialized across threads; canonical rendering and pixel comparison stay outside that lock. It requires exactly one page of the expected point dimensions; mismatches stay out of policy even under permissive pixel limits. No resizing or white-background flattening hides alpha or geometry loss.

The same visible-RGBA/hash criteria and report-only behavior described above apply. For an unexpected multi-page Canvas result, metrics observe its first page and the reported page count makes the verdict out of policy. PDF generation and requested comparison finish before opening the destination; missing/failed observation preserves an existing file. Native text/vectors and explained raster fragments are retained regardless of the fidelity verdict. Native PDF text is searchable vector content; this does not promise PowerPoint-style editing. Deck PDF comparison is rejected explicitly; export its Canvas slides individually. This observation does not establish PPTX or animation fidelity.

docs.title: Lottie reference player
docs.text:
The reference gate checks lottie-web 5.13.0 SVG and official Lottie Android 6.7.1, using Robolectric 4.17 NATIVE graphics, Android 15/API 35, mdpi and a software Drawable on Linux/JVM. Nine payloads validate against schema 1.0.1. Each player checks 37 canonical frames and detects 15 blank/frozen controls: the original 31+13 plus 6+2 covering multi-contour trim, changing contour lengths and shared translucent strokes. Both whole frames and artwork regions use channel tolerance 32, pixel difference ≤8%, and average-hash similarity ≥0.93. The shared-stroke interior RGBA probe permits at most two channel levels.

The web CI artifact also retains Android report.json, execution.json and maven.log, including failures. Native PNGs remain local to the job; rerun the same manifest with the command below to capture them. This tests the actual Android library/native graphics, not a device, emulator, ARM/GPU, iOS or app performance. Use the user guide for setup.

docs.title: Translucent fill/stroke investigation
docs.text:
An exploratory 960×640 multi-contour morph at frame 0 fails the Android ROI hash: (500,320)-(860,560) measures 0.921875 against 0.93, with pixel difference 3.2928% (within 8%). The full-frame hash is 1.0 and difference is 1.5653%. The same input exported again reproduces these values. Removing other layers or removing the morph animation gives the identical ROI result. Fill-only and stroke-only controls pass, and Android's combined output exactly equals drawing its isolated fill and then its isolated stroke.

In the combined ROI, all 2,845 pixels exceeding channel tolerance 32 lie outside flat alpha neighborhoods: among 65,459 pixels where both renderers' isolated fill/stroke alpha ranges span at most two levels in a 7×7 neighborhood, the maximum visible channel difference is two. This points toward paint-edge rasterization/compositing rather than morph length sampling; it does not identify a proven exporter defect or establish regression against an older exporter. The existing 52-case gate is unchanged. The opaque-fill morph and shared translucent-stroke fixtures remain independent checks.

To reproduce the combined artwork, use examples.lottie_trim_multi.build_canvas(), set only the layer with id="morph" to color="#159A8C40", and export with LottieOptions(fps=24, hold=0.5). Compare render_frame(0) with frame 0 of the Android renderer using the ROI and limits above. For controls, isolate that layer, remove animation, or remove just stroke/color respectively.

docs.title: Outlined-text admission
docs.text: The text compiler accepts static single-line printable ASCII, local nonvariable noncolor fonts and opaque solid paint. Layer opacity supplies translucency. Multi-character RAQM text needs explicit nonzero letter_spacing; unspaced BASIC text requires additive advances. Per-layer limits are 1,024 characters, 65,536 outline vertices and a 64 MiB font source. Geometry/precision/resource checks complete before writes; some require compiling intermediate animation samples.

docs.title: Web reference check
docs.text:
The developer check uses the actual lottie-web player in a disposable Chrome profile. It makes no player downloads, changes no export policies, and blocks browser HTTP/HTTPS requests while playing self-contained vectors.

From the repository root, install the locked development dependencies and the pinned test-only player, then select an existing Chrome executable:

uv sync --locked --extra lottie --dev
npm ci --prefix tests/fixtures/lottie/player --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
PYTHONPATH=. uv run --locked python scripts/check_lottie_fidelity.py \
  --chrome /path/to/chrome \
  --player tests/fixtures/lottie/player/node_modules/lottie-web/build/player/lottie.min.js \
  --output /tmp/quickthumb-lottie-observations

Node 24 and an existing Chrome are required; the output directory must be new. The report records schema/player hashes, browser/Node/player versions, export receipts, exact frame seeks, dimensions, whole-frame and artwork-region RGBA/hash metrics, and pass/fail results. Frames are captured at DPR 1 without resizing. PNG references, actual player PNGs and exported .lot files remain beside it.

The default gate uses the SVG renderer. Add --renderer canvas to investigate Canvas playback, or repeat --renderer to compare both. A failed comparison or an undetected blank/frozen control exits nonzero. Canvas opacity differences with the pinned player are a known failing comparison, not an accepted fallback.

docs.title: Android native graphics check
docs.text:
After generating the web manifest above, select an existing full JDK 21 and Maven 3.9+. Maven resolves pinned test-only Android/Robolectric dependencies from Maven Central and Google Maven; no Android SDK, device or product dependency is needed.

PYTHONPATH=. uv run --locked python scripts/check_lottie_android.py \
  --maven /path/to/mvn --java-home /path/to/jdk-21 \
  --cases /tmp/quickthumb-lottie-observations/cases.json \
  --output /tmp/quickthumb-android-observations

The output must be new. --settings accepts an existing Maven proxy/mirror setup; --trust-store selects an existing Java CA store, and --runtime-home selects a writable SDK cache. The actual Android parser consumes original bytes, without key reordering or another normalization. Frame seeks, render exceptions, native runtime identity and pixel/probe results are recorded in report.json beside PNGs and maven.log. A Maven success alone does not establish matching output: the Python gate checks the same budgets, controls and shared-paint pixel probe as the web check and exits nonzero on any unexpected result. iOS, physical Android devices and hardware rendering are outside this test.

docs.title: PPTX compatibility
docs.text:
PPTX keeps supported text and shapes editable. Glow can accompany that editable content as a fixed image; re-export after edits to update the glow. Outlined content may also require editing multiple objects together or re-exporting.

These effect combinations export the affected layer as a picture:

  • Translucent text, shapes or outlines with stroke/glow effects.
  • Gradient-filled shapes with stroke/glow effects.
  • Rich text with glow, or content combining glow and shadow.
  • Shape glow whose source extends beyond the slide.

Text with an opaque linear gradient can retain its editable fill and outline. Only the paint actually used by each text part determines whether it is translucent; unused or overridden colors do not remove editability.

Inspect canvas.validate_export("pptx") before export or the result's capability_report afterward to see compatibility decisions. A mixed editable foreground and fixed effect has support="partial"; a complete layer image has support="fallback". See document layer routing for receipt fields.

ExportPolicy(pptx={"title": "native"}) rejects these effect image or mixed representations for the layer with ID title. ExportPolicy(unsupported_motion="error") also rejects these effect fallbacks. Canvas and Deck to_pptx(policy=...) enforce the same policy checks as file exports. Defaults allow the explained fallbacks.

docs.title: HTML browser validation harness
docs.text:
The developer-only harness captures actual exported Canvas and two-slide Deck stages with an explicitly selected Chrome and Node's built-in WebSocket. It does not install a browser or change ExportPolicy:

PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/check_html_fidelity.py \
  --chrome "/path/to/chrome" --output /tmp/quickthumb-html-observations

The output directory must be new. Chrome runs headless with a temporary profile and loopback CDP; the harness never attaches to an existing browser session. It waits for fonts, images and slide transitions, captures only the original-size stage at DPR 1, and seeks a real click-triggered CSS fade at 0, 5 and 10 seconds. The report records browser/Node versions, canonical environment, input asset hashes, executed route diagnostics, dimensions, seek points, explicit fixture limits, pixel/hash metrics and verdicts. Canonical/browser PNGs remain beside it.

The mixed text/shape/image/mask fixtures allow a channel tolerance of 16, at most 8% differing pixels, and average-hash similarity of at least 0.94. Every component must also satisfy its recorded region criteria: text allows 20% differing pixels and requires hash similarity 0.95; the native ellipse allows 2% and requires 0.98. The embedded image is exact; the masked fragment allows only one channel level of rounding. Text/ellipse channel tolerance is 16. These local criteria prevent small missing features from passing a whole-stage average. Negative controls remove each text/image/mask/ellipse element in both the wide Canvas and tall Deck and must fail that specific region, not merely another metric. All allowances are fixture-specific and are not general document budgets. The simple fade permits only one channel level of rounding; a deliberately wrong document must fail comparison. Unexpected verdicts fail the command while retaining its report. No automatic raster fallback or browser/CI installation is performed.

This observes one Chrome/font/platform environment and one bounded CSS animation, not every browser, animation, cue, or Deck transition. CairoSVG cannot substitute for this browser observation. Existing Node runtime tests check scheduling and state behavior separately from browser pixels.

docs.title: Static cross-export checks
docs.text:
tests/test_static_export_matrix.py sends the same authored content through the public Canvas and Deck file-export boundaries. The first 160×120 slide combines repository-font text, a native rectangle, a generated image and an elliptical mask; the second Deck slide has a translucent rectangle on a transparent canvas. The checks distinguish measured appearance from structural evidence:

Format Canvas Deck Capability and fallback evidence PNG Decoded RGBA equals the canonical sample Each numbered slide equals its canonical sample Raster output; no native-object or document-viewer claim SVG Actual CairoSVG observation plus native text/vector and PNG checks Single-file Deck SVG is rejected; each Canvas slide is measured separately Executed source IDs, native routes and explained image/mask PNG routes HTML Stage markup, native text/CSS and exact mask PNG Stage count and slide-local routes Structural only; no browser pixel measurement in this matrix PDF Actual PDFium observation, searchable text, vector paths and image objects Page count/geometry, native objects and rendered component regions Canvas routes reported; Deck executed routes and receipt fidelity are not collected yet PPTX Editable OOXML text/shapes and exact positioned mask PNG Slide count and per-slide native/raster objects Executed routes reported; PowerPoint/Keynote appearance remains unmeasured

The mixed SVG/PDF fixture uses explicit whole-image limits: zero channel tolerance, at most 8% different pixels, and hash similarity of at least 0.94. These are fixture-specific font/edge budgets, not export defaults. Native text must also be present as text, and small rectangle, image and mask-interior regions must match exactly so a missing component cannot hide in the whole-image budget. The text region also requires hash similarity of at least 0.95 and permits at most 30% different pixels after a channel tolerance of 16 for font rasterization edges. A real Deck PDF containing searchable white-on-white text must fail this regional check, even though its text objects and other component regions are intact. For the transparent rectangle only, alpha must match exactly while visible RGB may differ by at most two levels per channel because of renderer premultiplication/unpremultiplication rounding. Fully hidden RGB follows the existing visible-RGBA comparison rule; PNG still preserves raw RGBA exactly. No output is resized or flattened onto an invented matte.

Run uv run --locked pytest tests/test_static_export_matrix.py --no-cov -q. The existing quality workflow already runs this file through pytest tests/ with the SVG/PDF/PPTX extras and native Cairo installed. Local environments without an optional observer skip its cases with the dependency reason. Pytest case IDs identify the format and document kind. Each case keeps its source JSON, canonical PNGs, actual exports and JSON receipts in its temporary directory; measured receipts include renderer versions, canonical environment, limits and metrics. A failure is reproducible from the shared fixture and named format check rather than a platform-specific screenshot baseline.

This is a bounded static matrix. It does not run a browser, certify PPTX viewer pixels/fonts/timing, or add a Deck PDF fidelity policy. The separate HTML browser harness and native presentation-viewer observations require their own execution and environment evidence. Structural success must not be reported as a rendered pixel-fidelity verdict.

docs.title: Inspecting complex layouts
docs.text: For the standard inspection API, see Canvas inspection and Document inspection.

docs.title: Parent-linked scenes
docs.text:
When inspecting parent-linked hierarchies or running canvas.diagnose():

  • Authored-static bounds: Layer bounding boxes describe their static layout coordinates in world space.
  • Null controllers: Null controller layers (Canvas.null()) act as invisible transformation points and do not produce visual bounding boxes.
  • Visual debug overlay: Use canvas.render("debug.png", debug=True) to visualize the exact bounding boxes measured for each layer.

docs.title: Groups and clipped boundaries
docs.text:
• Group bounding boxes: A group's measured bounding box encloses all of its children, accounting for gaps, padding, and any attached clips or masks.
  • Nested clips and masks: Clips and masks applied to parent groups or descendant layers constrain their visible area without altering relative layout coordinates.
  • Animated counters: Intrinsic counter text layers (Canvas.counter()) calculate bounding boxes based on their settled final value, ensuring layout stability throughout playback.

docs.title: Animation timing reference
docs.text:
For a concise guide, see Animation timing.

Use seconds for authored motion, slide durations, holds, video placement and caption cues. sample() observes the canonical timeline; export() reports the visual timeline actually encoded. Those measurements serve different purposes.

docs.title: Choose the clock
docs.text:
Output or observation Timing contract sample() with no time or fps One authored-static frame per Canvas/page, matching raster output without seeking an animation endpoint; duration=0, frame time=None. sample(time=...) Observe explicit document times. Slide windows are [start, end); an exact boundary belongs to the incoming slide. Times beyond the end show the settled final scene. sample(fps=...) Observe a uniform grid 0, 1/fps, 2/fps, … before the timeline end. A zero-length timeline is still observed once at zero. GIF Silent, variable frame durations in 10 ms steps; identical frames can coalesce. Default sampling rate 20 fps; supported rate is greater than zero and at most 100 fps. MP4 / WebM / MOV Constant-rate encoded frames, including repeated held frames. Default 30 fps; supported rate is greater than zero and at most 120 fps. HTML Browser-driven, interactive cues and slide navigation. No encoded fps or fixed total playback duration, and no Deck narration playback.

GifOptions.fps and VideoOptions.fps request the sampling density. Moving spans are sampled within their own timing boundaries; static spans become held shots. Video allocates repeated frames on a cumulative frame clock, while GIF quantizes cumulative durations to centiseconds. A canonical uniform sample grid is therefore not an index into the encoded file: arbitrary fractional spans, palette/lossy encoding and duplicate-frame coalescing can change frame positions or counts.

Read ExportResult.timing_metrics after an animated export:

Field Meaning fps The selected sampling rate; for GIF this is not stored frames divided by playback duration. frame_count Frames actually encoded, after GIF coalescing or video hold repetition. duration Encoded visual playback seconds: summed GIF delays or video frame count divided by fps. Audio container padding can differ.

FrameSequence.duration instead describes the unquantized canonical timeline. HTML returns no fixed playback timing in timing_metrics; its zero duration is not a claim that its interactive animations take no time.

from quickthumb import AnimationSpec, Canvas, GifOptions

canvas = Canvas(160, 90).background(color="#000000").shape(
    "rectangle", (40, 20), 80, 50, "#FF0000",
    animation=AnimationSpec.fade(duration=1),
)
samples = canvas.sample(fps=7, hold=0.37)
result = canvas.export("timed.gif", animation=GifOptions(fps=7, hold=0.37))
print(samples.duration, len(samples.frames))
print(result.timing_metrics.model_dump())

docs.title: Temporal exposure
docs.text:
Opt into centered motion blur when exporting a Canvas or Deck:

from quickthumb import MotionBlur, VideoOptions

canvas.export(
    "exposure.mp4",
    animation=VideoOptions(fps=30, motion_blur=MotionBlur(samples=8, shutter_angle=180)),
)

GifOptions and ImageSequenceOptions accept the same setting. None is the only off setting; MotionBlur accepts 2–64 samples and a positive shutter angle up to 360 degrees. The shutter spans (angle / 360) / fps seconds around each rendered frame. Instants outside the document timeline use its boundary state. Hard cuts bound the exposure to the slide on the center's side of the cut; an exact cut time belongs to the incoming slide. Smooth transitions participate in the exposure, including samples on either side of their start time. Video and image-sequence exposure centers follow the output grid index / fps; GIF centers follow its variable-duration shot clock. The encoded-sRGB premultiplied channels are averaged before returning straight RGBA, preserving saturated colors in transparent trails.

Exposure also integrates timed captions and appearances. They can contribute within half a shutter window of a cue boundary. Authored cue times and playback length remain unchanged; GIF delays and video frame counts still follow their codec clocks. With zero hold, the last frame is an exposure of motion. Add a hold to show an entirely settled frame.

This setting supports Canvas and Deck GIF/video exports and image sequences, including workers. Each worker computes a complete exposure with the same sample times and alpha accumulation as serial rendering. Direct byte helpers do not support this setting. sample() and render_frame() remain instantaneous canonical observations. Export receipts identify the requested temporal exposure in their capability report; source inspection cannot infer an export-only setting.

docs.title: Support and receipts
docs.text:
capabilities_for(target)["motion_blur"] declares temporal-exposure support:

Target family Support Meaning video full Canvas/Deck MP4, WebM, MOV and image sequences integrate the exposure. raster partial, static fallback Animated GIF integrates it; static raster files have no exposure window. html, pptx unsupported, static fallback Exposure is ignored; the authored browser/PowerPoint motion remains unchanged.

VideoOptions/GifOptions belong to their animated output families; passing them to HTML/PPTX raises an option-family error. The capability table does not make those options silently accepted. inspect_motion() reports source-authored features and does not claim that export-only blur was enabled. After an actual export, find the motion_blur row in result.capability_report for the applied sample count and angle; timing_metrics retains the encoded playback facts. Image-sequence results carry the same applied row and their frame/duration facts.

Run the moving-marker example to write matching OFF/8-sample GIFs. Its scene also drives the controlled sample-cost benchmark.

docs.title: Slide duration and transitions
docs.text:
Layer motion and the incoming transition start on the same slide clock. For noninteractive media, on_click cues run in sequence like after_previous; with_previous cues overlap. Delays are part of those clocks. Transitions play over the previous slide's settled scene; a slide without an explicit transition starts instantly on the first slide and uses a 0.5-second crossfade thereafter. Use Cut() for an immediate boundary.

A slide's exit is determined by the latest applicable boundary:

  • With neither a duration override nor advance_after, transition and layer motion finish, then the settled scene holds for hold seconds (default 3).
  • For Deck video, slide(duration=...) sets a total slide window, including its transition and motion. Without an explicit duration, narration supplies that window. Neither trims a longer visual animation; the slide lasts long enough for both. Narration itself is trimmed or padded to its scheduled window.
  • A transition's advance_after replaces hold: its boundary is counted after the incoming transition. The exit is the latest of that boundary, completed motion and any narration/explicit duration. For example, a one-second animation with Cut(advance_after=0.1) ends at one second even when hold=3; it does not add a three-second tail.

GIF ignores Deck narration and slide(duration=...); it uses motion, transitions, advance_after and hold. Deck.sample() uses the narration-aware video schedule, so a narrated Deck's GIF need not match its sampled duration.

The encoder shows the settled state even with hold=0, replacing the final motion shot when needed rather than always appending a full hold. A static or sub-frame slide still needs a representable frame. GIF and video durations can therefore differ slightly from the mathematical timeline. Deck video currently requires a positive hold for slides with neither narration nor an explicit positive duration; a zero hold remains valid for Canvas and Deck GIF.

docs.title: Audio, captions and reduced motion
docs.text:
MP4/WebM/MOV mix supported clip audio, Deck narration and an optional soundtrack. Narration starts at its slide's absolute offset. The soundtrack is trimmed to the visual timeline and can loop; audio padding from the codec does not extend the reported visual duration. GIF and image sequences carry no audio. Use video when the soundtrack or narration must accompany the motion. MP4 exports play layer animations and transitions while retaining per-slide narration. For still-slide narration, author static canvases and set deck.transition(Cut()).

A video layer's start is slide-local. Its trim_start, trim_end and speed select source media time; caption start/end are relative to the placed clip, not to the original source file. Captions are active over [start, end) and are burned into the foreground of supported raster/video output. They remain timed when reduced motion freezes the clip's picture.

ExportPolicy(reduced_motion=True) suppresses authored layer motion and authored slide transitions. It retains holds, narration and caption timing; default Deck crossfades can remain between slides. Use the actual export receipt for the resulting duration, rather than the original motion duration.

HTML keeps on_click cues interactive and after_previous cues automatic. advance_after enables conditional auto-advance after the incoming transition; it does not turn the presentation into fixed-duration video. Video layers use a static fallback in HTML, so their playback/caption timing is not reproduced. Check validate_export() and the returned fallback diagnostics for the target. GIF/video option families, unsupported transparency and codec rate limits fail with actionable errors rather than silently selecting another format.

docs.title: Verify playback
docs.text:
The three-slide integration scene in tests/test_video_layers.py checks actual GIF, MP4 and WebM output: selected pixels against canonical samples, incoming transitions, caption start/end windows, encoded timing, and decoded soundtrack and narration frequencies. Reduced-motion cases check frozen clip imagery and timed captions. Run it with FFmpeg and ffprobe installed:

uv run --locked pytest tests/test_video_layers.py -k motion_package --no-cov

Existing HTML timeline tests execute the JavaScript in Node stage fixtures; target-specific browser fidelity remains a separate check.

docs.title: Quickthumb 0.8.0
docs.text:
Quickthumb 0.8.0 brings the work since v0.7.0 into one release: a shared Canvas/Deck output contract, more precise animation, vector paths, text selectors, compositing, bounded Lottie export, and a unified presentation UI. This is a breaking pre-1.0 release. Read the migration section before upgrading saved specs, scripts, or integrations.

Jump to migration from v0.7.0.

python -m pip install --upgrade "quickthumb[cli]==0.8.0"

Python 3.11+ is required. Video export needs an external FFmpeg installation; installing a Python extra does not install native programs or libraries.

docs.title: One document and output workflow
docs.text:
Canvas and Deck now implement the structural Document protocol with validate(), inspect(), diagnose(), prefetch_assets(), sample(), and export(). There is no new document wrapper to construct.

from quickthumb import Canvas, Deck, VideoOptions

canvas = Canvas(320, 180).background(color="#102030").shape(
    "rectangle", position=(24, 24), width=96, height=64, color="#42CEB7",
)
receipt = canvas.export("card.png")
print(receipt.written_paths, receipt.pixel_metrics.width)
frames = canvas.sample(time=[0.0])
print(frames.frames[0].sha256)
Deck(slides=[canvas]).export("slides.mp4", animation=VideoOptions(hold=1.0))
  • export(path, ...) is the recommended file API and returns ExportResult: written paths, capability/fallback diagnostics, pixel and timing metrics, assets, and the observed render environment. render() remains available; it does not return a receipt. Both enforce the shared file-option and capability policy. Byte/string to_*() methods retain their own contracts.
  • sample() returns FrameSequence / CanonicalFrame data from the canonical renderer. inspect_document() combines layout, motion, diagnostics, and observed assets without writing an export.
  • Canonical to_json() / from_json() now cover both document kinds and plugin references. JSON describes the authored scene, not exported frames, callbacks, fonts, or an asset archive. Report models have model_dump_json().
  • Structured errors expose code and details with input paths and layer context. InputError, MissingAssetError, and ErrorDetail join the existing Quickthumb error types. Validation and diagnostic reports are JSON-safe.

Ordinary files may overwrite existing files. Deck raster output writes numbered slide files, reported in the receipt; this is not an atomic multi-file transaction. Unknown suffixes, incompatible option families, and unsupported format overrides are rejected. Explicit raster format overrides support PNG/JPEG/WebP without renaming the supplied path. JPEG quality is 1–95 and ordinary WebP quality is 1–100; PNG does not accept compression quality here.

Output contract · Public API · JSON/schema

docs.title: Animation, audio, and rendering
docs.text:
• Transform sampling uses subpixel affine geometry. anchor is a normalized 0–1 pivot, separate from layout align; ScaleXTrack and ScaleYTrack add independent axes. Image ScaleTrack now scales the outer object, like other layers. ImageZoomTrack and image pan/Ken Burns controls address content inside the image viewport. Static and animated transform handling is aligned.
  • PositionKeyframeSpec adds Bézier handles and constant-speed path sampling. Position values offset authored placement; handles offset their own keyframe, rather than declaring absolute canvas control points. Absolute TimingSpec.start values now survive JSON round trips. auto_orient adds path heading to authored rotation/rotation tracks, independent of track order. ColorTrack uses perceptual text/shape paint interpolation.
  • CubicBezierEasing, per-keyframe easing, hold keyframes, closed-form SpringEasing, and seeded, band-limited Wiggle expand motion authoring. Springs use a normalized one-second response with exact endpoints. Wiggle preserves the authored start and freezes its final perturbation after motion.
  • Canvas.null() / NullLayer and parent support scene-local transform hierarchies, including bounded nested group composition, counters, clips, and masks. .group() remains the simple auto-layout entry point. Parent-local placement does not change percentage coordinates into parent percentages: they still resolve against the canvas. Unsupported compositions are diagnosed.
  • Word/line staggering uses placed text layout. RangeSelector supports weighted selection and animated bounds; character targets are Unicode code points, not grapheme clusters. A requested exact fragment is rendered or rejected before output, including a single target; there is no approximate split path.
  • quickthumb.audio.analyze_audio() returns cached AudioAnalysis source-clock onset times and relative RMS windows. Use onsets as numeric timing anchors or analysis.scale_track() in AnimationSpec.timeline(). This is transient detection, not beat tracking, and does not attach a soundtrack for you.
  • Video sampling respects decoded timestamps; caption boundaries and encoded output clocks are tested separately from canonical scene time. Times are in seconds. GIF quantization and codec timing can differ from the canonical grid; receipts report timing rather than promising identical clocks in every codec.
  • GIF/video frame streaming, static-slide-prefix reuse, shared font faces, and bounded spawn-based frame workers reduce repeated work. workers=1 is the default; supported multi-worker output accepts 1–8 workers. Use render_quality="high" for spatial supersampling. Optional MotionBlur adds temporal exposure to file options and image sequences, not byte methods. It is distinct from spatial quality and has explicit composition limits. to_gif() also exposes proportional max_size and palette colors (2–256), previously available through GifOptions at the file boundary.

Motion and timing · Audio API and examples · Kinetic lower third

docs.title: Paths, masks, and plugins
docs.text:
• Canvas.path() / PathLayer author SVG path data in a fixed viewport: polygonal paths, adaptive quadratic/cubic curves and elliptical arcs, bounded gradient fills, solid/dashed strokes, caps and joins. Animated geometry is repainted at device resolution. DashOffsetTrack, TrimStartTrack, TrimEndTrack, and TrimOffsetTrack use canonical path-length sampling.
  • PathMorphTrack interpolates matched path contours. This is a different API from the existing cross-slide transitions.Morph; it does not imply every vector exporter can consume a morph track.
  • TrackMatte supports alpha/luma sources with explicit source visibility, inversion, and reuse rules. Owner-local path masks and MaskPositionTrack, MaskSizeTrack, and MaskFeatherTrack extend masking. Nested/dynamic group, caption, backdrop, and other unsupported combinations are rejected rather than silently approximated. Native HTML hard masks have narrower support than raster.
  • Versioned PluginDefinition / PluginRegistry registrations declare parameters, assets, and synchronous raster callbacks. Canvas.plugin() and JSON loading accept an explicit registry. Plugins are trusted Python, not a sandbox; JSON does not install callbacks. Raster rendering is required; timed plugins and plugin rendering with workers > 1 are not supported. Optional SVG hooks affect SVG only and require local pixel admission to be used as native output.

Path API · Masks and mattes · Plugin contract

docs.title: Output formats and their boundaries
docs.text:
Output What changes in 0.8.0 PNG/JPEG/WebP Shared file policy, receipts, explicit quality validation; still raster output. Image sequence export_image_sequence() writes PNG, JPEG, or WebP frames and a manifest to a new directory. Existing directories, even empty ones, are not overwritten. The parent must exist. Publication uses private staging and an exclusive atomic rename; it is not a crash-durable asset archive. No audio is included. GIF/MP4 Shared animation clock and output controls. Deck MP4 plays animation by default and retains per-slide narration and soundtrack scheduling. MP4 is opaque; GIF has palette/transparency limits. WebM/MOV transparent=True supports VP9 alpha WebM and ProRes 4444 MOV. Alpha support is not a promise of exact lossless RGB/RGBA across codec color conversion or players. MOV needs FFmpeg's prores_ks. SVG Native bounded path/paint and admitted plugin routes; receipts distinguish actual native and raster layers. Static fidelity observation uses CairoSVG. No Deck to_svg() method. HTML Presentation remains interactive; supported native path stroke phase/trim and hard-mask mappings are bounded. Path motion mapping uses a 120 Hz sampling grid plus authored knots. Unsupported animation has explicit static/fallback reporting, including per-slide Deck routes. PDF Bounded paths become editable curves with explicit raster fallback for unsupported paint. Optional PDFium comparisons report actual executed routes. Deck PDF fidelity observation is rejected. PPTX Receipts report actual editable/raster routes; support is feature-specific. Native PowerPoint playback/fidelity has not been certified by the Linux test suite. Lottie .lot Canvas only, via export()/render() and LottieOptions; no Deck or byte API. Bounded solid paints on shapes/paths (including alpha), cubic geometry, native stroke trim, sampled held poses, Null/Shape parent hierarchies, and self-contained static ASCII text outlines with opaque text paint. No general raster fallback, audio, images, gradients, arbitrary text shaping, track mattes, or PathMorphTrack consumer. Unsupported features error even when another policy asks to rasterize. 
from quickthumb import ImageSequenceOptions, LottieOptions

canvas.export_image_sequence(
    "frames", format="webp", lossless=True,
    options=ImageSequenceOptions(fps=30.0, hold=1.0),
)
canvas.export("card.lot", animation=LottieOptions(fps=30.0, hold=1.0))

Image sequence encoding arguments are separate from timing: PNG preserves canonical 8-bit straight RGBA; JPEG flattens to RGB over a default white matte; WebP can be lossy or lossless. Sequence JPEG/WebP quality is 1–95, unlike ordinary WebP's 1–100. lossless is WebP-only; incompatible parameters error. The manifest records encoding, frame names/count/timing, dimensions, alpha, mode, quality/lossless/matte accurately instead of asserting universal RGBA equality.

ExportPolicy makes unsupported-motion handling explicit. Native-route reports are observations of the route taken, not editability guarantees in all viewers. Opt-in static SVG/PDF fidelity limits are report-only: exceeding a limit does not automatically reject or switch renderers. Chrome comparison is a test tool, not a new production rendering backend. See the format-specific limits.

docs.title: Assets, fonts, CLI, and presentation
docs.text:
• Shared remote resolution adds prefetch_assets() and manifests with cache state, source/content identity, and stale reasons. Offline cached rendering is explicit; stale data is reported, not automatically refused. A document retains its first remote resolution; a new document resolves again under the current cache policy. Reports do not transfer bytes or own cache lifetimes. Keep local files and referenced cache files available through export. Cache controls are QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_CACHE_DIR, QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_MAX_AGE, and QUICKTHUMB_ASSET_OFFLINE.
  • Render environments record actual font bytes, face/variation/shaping identity, and renderer versions. Remote fonts use content-addressed copies. Default QUICKTHUMB_DEFAULT_FONT selection now honors weight, bold, and italic, so existing text can change wrapping, alignment, and visible pixels.
  • quickthumb doctor checks discovered requirements and write readiness; quickthumb inspect provides a common Canvas/Deck envelope. Schema, lint, render, and error output follow the stricter document contract. CLI raster quality follows the JPEG 1–95 / WebP 1–100 distinction.
  • quickthumb serve keeps slides-first presentation as the default. Presentation and Inspect motion share warm-white/teal chrome, real slide thumbnails, and the original slide aspect ratio. The motion panel scrubs export-renderer raster frames with timing/proxy controls; it is not playback, audio, or an editor. --timeline opens that inspection mode. Presenter view now matches the theme, with current/next slides, notes, elapsed time, and navigation. Keyboard/cue progression, audience synchronization, and source reload remain.
  • Installation/docs now distinguish base output from cli, svg, pdf, pptx, lottie, and rembg extras. CairoSVG needs native Cairo; text outlines need [lottie]/fontTools and supported fonts (RAQM for nonzero letter spacing). Background removal may download its model on first use.
  • Security/dependency maintenance includes patched rembg/ONNX Runtime, Pillow, certifi, filelock/virtualenv, and ty 0.0.84, plus current pinned CI actions, watchfiles, Typer, inline-snapshot, and diff-cover. Existing scan gates remain.

Installation · CLI and serve · Examples

docs.title: Migration from v0.7.0
docs.text:
No compatibility aliases are provided for removed entry points.

Before 0.8.0 deck.to_animated_mp4(slide_duration=2.0) deck.to_mp4(hold=2.0); files use deck.export("out.mp4", animation=VideoOptions(hold=2.0)). deck.to_mp4(...) / deck.render_mp4(...) for static narrated PNG slides General MP4 now plays motion. Use static canvases and explicit transitions.Cut() for cuts; narration/duration remain on .slide(). The old still-only method is removed, not silently preserved. deck.to_gif(slide_duration=2.0) / deck.to_webm(slide_duration=2.0) Use hold=2.0 on either method. Update saved animation option JSON too. Iterating canvas.diagnose() / deck.diagnose() directly Iterate .diagnose().findings; DiagnosticReport replaces the old result shapes. deck.model_dump(mode="json") json.loads(deck.to_json()) for scene data. Result/report models still have Pydantic serialization. Handwritten JSON without document kind, or with unknown fields/duplicate layer IDs Add kind: "canvas" / "deck" at document boundaries (including slides), retain layer type, and fix invalid fields/IDs. Regenerate schema with the installed version. Strict parsing also rejects non-finite/trailing JSON and malformed scalar fields. Treating image ScaleTrack as viewport zoom Use ImageZoomTrack for viewport zoom; ScaleTrack transforms the outer image geometry. Review anchors and auto-orient plus rotation offsets. Importing timeline/compiler/renderer helpers from quickthumb Use documented authoring types and document sample() / inspect_motion() operations. Low-level implementation helpers are no longer root-level public exports or a supported lifecycle. Assuming default font style selects the regular face Select a font/style deliberately and review layout after the corrected style lookup.

For a static narrated cut sequence in the general MP4 path:

from quickthumb import Deck, VideoOptions, transitions

deck = Deck(320, 180, transition=transitions.Cut())
deck.slide(canvas, audio="narration.wav", duration=2.0)
deck.export("narrated.mp4", animation=VideoOptions(fps=30.0, hold=1.0))
mp4_bytes = deck.to_mp4(fps=30.0, hold=1.0)

duration overrides narration length, which otherwise supplies the static slide's duration before the default hold is used. This does not freeze an arbitrary animated Canvas. A None transition uses the existing default fade; use an explicit Cut for cuts. Reduced-motion handling is a separate policy.

For integrations built against unreleased intermediate checkouts, also replace export_png_sequence / PngSequence* with export_image_sequence / ImageSequence*, animation option quality with render_quality, and to_narrated_mp4 / render_narrated_mp4 with the general MP4 path. Those intermediate narrated/sequence names were not v0.7.0 public APIs. A monkeypatched render() hook is no longer a dispatch mechanism for export().

docs.title: Validation and remaining limits
docs.text:
The pre-release integrated main passed Linux CI with 4,632 tests passed, 3 skipped, coverage 92.23%, and quality/type/build/security checks. The version PR and published wheel are checked separately by the release pipeline. Reference-player and pixel evidence exists for the documented bounded Lottie, HTML, vector, timing, and alpha routes; this does not certify every combination or native application.

The outstanding Linux default-font golden refresh is not newly verified by this release. Format-specific implementation and native-application limits are listed with each output above.

Full comparison: https://github.com/sjquant/quickthumb/compare/v0.7.0...v0.8.0

# Simplified from examples/orbit_atlas.py
canvas = Canvas(WIDTH, HEIGHT).image(

slides = deck()

이미지, 프레젠테이션, 동영상을 Python으로 만듭니다. 레이아웃을 코드로 남겨 두고, 사진과 제목을 바꿔 다시 쓸 수 있습니다.
